review_text: Went to universal this september. What a waste of money. The whole park is one big commercial circus with just a few average rides on it. The staff is extremly rude and the lines are short at first site, but once you line up outside one of the attractions, you'll discover that the line inside the buildings is many times longer than you can see. This park charges the same prices as Disney but not even half the fun. If you're planning to go to Orlando and have money to spent, you better go to Disney!

We had a week-long break and decided to head to Orlando. Our fist stop was Universal studios on a Sunday morning at the end of June. We hardly waited in a line to get in and headed into the Universal Stuiods Park first. It was amazing for two country bumpkins like us. The streets were virtually deserted at opening time and we only waited in line at Shrek 4D. It was well worth it and yes, we did that one twice. I wish I could say the same about Twister. They promise a thrill, as close to a tornado as you could wish to get. Needless to say my hair hardly moved and the so-called tornado rushing through was more like a breeze, but I guess with all the kids in the room we couldn't expect anything more. Islands of Adventure was Great, even if you don't like thrill rides. We did the Jurassic Park ride - much to my husband's dread as he hates anything "fast". Sometimes I think it's more fun watching other people on some of theses rides. we did that "fast line" thing where you get a ticket and come back at the allocated time. That was fabulous, especially since it was so hot that we had time inbetween rides to get an ice cold drink. Yes, we did manage to do four theme parks in five days including Universal, Disney, Sea World and Nasa - Florida truly is a wonderful place and I can recommend it to anyone who has a couple of days off and nowhere to go. Oh, the Raddison Park Hotel was fantastic - organised busses to all the theme parks every morning. Well worth the stay.

We took our 4 and 6 year old to Universal, knowing that it was more of an adult oriented park.. We did not realize, however, that there was only ONE ride they would enjoy, which was ET. My six year old son was so frightened by the rides that he would not sleep in his own room that night. (Something he has not done since he was 2!) My husband, who can ride any roller coaster, got sick from riding the Back to the Future Ride. The "subtle" insults to Disney on the rides and by the staff members not only show how unprofessional Universal is, but how threatened they must feel by a more superior theme park. Don't waste your time and money taking any child under 10 to Universal. Islands of Adventure may be better, but I am going to save my money for my Disney tickets. We will not be back!!!

I have to agree with the one traveler who stated it was outdated. For the price of tickets, I guess I had my expectations too high. The rides there were so-so - nothing great. The mummy is probably the best ride there. I chose to go to Universal over MGM b/c I thought it would be better, now I'm not so sure. We just weren't impressed and didn't spend a whole day there like we had planned.

My fiance and 9 year old son spent Dec 20-26 in Orlando going to Universal and Islands of Adventure. I was worried it wouldnt come close to DISNEY but we had a GREAT TIME. THE MUMMY IS NOW OUR FAVORITE RIDE EVER , hit the singles line to ride quickly and as many times as you want. All the rides were great except Back to the Furure , I'd skip that. Customer service wasnt that great but the attractions were awesome. City Walk-Hard Rock, Margaritaville etc were great also.

There are so many reasons to hate this park. The "rides" were very short and the lines very long. (We got there very early on a Friday in April.) Paying $70 per person to get into the park, makes you a second class citizen waiting in line. You can buy an "express pass" which allows you to jump in line. After waiting 10-20 minutes in line, we watched as "express pass" holders walked up and walked in ahead of us. This of course made our wait longer. We started off with the Men in Black ride, which involved using play laser guns to shoot "rubber aliens" sitting in garbage cans and around corners. The car you ride in spins a few times which is the really big excitement. Then the ride broke leaving us locked into our seats for about 30 minutes until the staff finally shut off the ride then came and led us out of the ride. Twister was realistic but again, very short. For each ride we went on, the exit forced you through a gift shop, which was irritating. If I want to go into the gift shop, I will. This park seems to be geared toward children but the rides are based on movies primarily from the 1970s to the early 1990s. In fairness, we were not able to get into the Terminator, Earthquake or Mummy rides/shows. I had heard those were quite good. For those, the lines were so long (35+ minutes) we did not wait. I am used to waited for rides but these were oh so not worth the effort. You will be acosted by people taking surveys for tv shows. We were stopped six times. This park promotes itself as taking people behind the scenes of movies/tv shows. In reality, it is little more than a bunch of concocted, poorly designed, cheaply conceived ride/show experiences. Why create a park like this? Universal Studios is a cynical money grab by Universal/NBC to try to wring a few more bucks out of its tired media properties. Stick with the mouse.

There is no good place to start. Do not even think about going to the rides in Islands of Adventure. They over hype and over sell it to the point of fights breaking out in some lines. My family and I PERSONALLY witnessed a kid in line at the Spider Man ride urinating in a corner because he couldnt hold it anymore. There was absolutely NO staff in the area that could help him and no way for the family to get the kid out in time. People would not budge! The father had to physically push his way through other people waiting in line who just flat out refused to move. The posted wait time when we entered the line was 60 minutes. 104 minutes later we got on the ride. The park just failed to staff the ride properly.  It did get better at night with the Blue Man Group show. The theater was great and the show was ideal for kids! I would go back to that show in a minute!

We had two children with us when we visited Universal. I can say that had it been just adults it would have been a decent time but this park is just not very geared towards children. Yes, there are areas within the park that cater to little ones (though not too little, children under 5 years old would be hard pressed to find many rides they can go on) but overall having children with you won't work at this park. You are going to walk about a mile to get from the parking structures to the actual park entrance. They advertise motorized walkways but many were not on during the 3 days we went there. Then you are going to stand in ride for about an hour to go one a 90 second ride (hope the kids are patient to stand outside waiting for the adults since they cannot go on most of the rides). Also, DO NOT FALL FOR THE MEAL PASS. You pay $20.00 for an all you can eat for one day pass but there is only 4 places in the place that accept the pass and it takes about 40 minutes to get through the line to get food. Then the people that work at the places where you eat are nasty about portions and won't let you have enough to feed yourself and insist that you go through the 40 minute line again to get a (free) dessert to go with your dinner. All in all, you may have time and get a chance to eat about $10 worth of food and that is if you are willing to spend 90 minutes in a restaurant for each meal -which cuts time out of the day for standing in line at rides. You have to go through the 40 minute line just to get a free refill on your soda! NOT WORTH IT! If you are a family with kids go to Disney's Magic Kingdom. We were there for a 4 hour evening event (Pirate and Princess Party) and went on the same number of rides that we go to go on during 3 days at Universal. Plus, Disney had rides that little ones could go on. Skip Universal unless it is a really slow time of year. The staff is rude and can't muster a smile to save their lives and the lines are long. The food pass is a rip off.

So - After spending (1) day in Island of Adventure, and (1) day in Universal Studios:  11/25/08: Island Of Adventures: Good time. A few good Roller Coasters. Some of the rides need to be updated, but over all we had a good time.  11/26/08: Universal Studios: Terrible. The ride are SO dated... ET is still a ride, but the people I went with (ages 18 to 13) didn't know who that was. MIB: 3rd rate, compared to rides that are out there where you 'shoot things'. "Mummy's" OK, but only because ALL the other rides were so out-dated/boring.  Also: we were a group of 6. During the day we were told by staff things like "You are to many, and you are messing up the order" "You need to split up, to make it easier on us". We were also YELLED AT twice. You know those pictures they take of you, and then try to sell you? Well, I take a snap shot of them - I do this all the time at Disney. They are pictures of me... In Disney - NO ONE has ever said anything to me. At Universal - one guy YELLED at me.  Universal isn't worth the $$$ to spend - traveling all that way to Florida to go to a 6-Flags type park isn't worth it. Spend the extra $$ In Disney, or some other park.  I welcome a feed back from Universal, dont expect one.

We visited with a 3-day combination pass for Universal and Islands of Adventure, with EXPRESS PASS, AND the MEAL DEAL included . All FREE for a bonus trip through my husbands company. YES...a great experience but I have a few things to point out. You MUST get the EXPRESS PASS if you are going to truly enjoy this park! I actually felt GUILTY walking to the head of the lines at times, and getting right on the rides! But if you DON'T have the pass, you waste SO much time waiting...up to 90 minutes waiting in line for a 3 minute long ride!! Life is TOO short! The MEAL DEAL is a good value...but the choices that they give are ALL JUNK FOOD!!! We had been doing the South Beach diet prior to our visit and it was simply IMPOSSIBLE to eat within the rules!! Pizza, nuggets, burgers, fries, desserts..and NO drinks included. We will SURVIVE three days of junk, but I am NOT looking forward to getting on the scales tomorrow after all of my hard work over the previous 3 weeks!!  Rides to NOT miss: Woody Woodpecker's Nuthouse Coaster....the BEST for the kids AND Parents!! Simpsons...Jimmy Neutron... E.T. . .(DEFINITE MUST!!!)... The Animal Actors on Location....it's a live animal show...they loved it! JAWS....LOUD, SMELLY, HOT, and somewhat scarey for a 5 and 7 year old. Somewhat entertaining for us adults that grew up watching the JAWS movies!!  Didn't get the chance to do Twister and Disaster...too intense for the kids...would liked to have done Shrek 4 D....no help on these.  Bottom line...get Express Pass, (it is included with some of the nearby hotels like Hard Rock Hotel)....GO EARLY, buy it with the combo pass to Islands of Adventure which is more catered to young children! Take a lanyard (strap around your neck with a clear see through pouch) for the Express passes...you need to show them again and again. Wear cool clothes and comfortable sneakers with socks!! Have fun!!!!

What a waste of time and money. For the fortune it cost to get in and the WAY TOO HIGH cost of a Fast Pass, that isn't fast at all, you would be better off going somewhere else. In fact anywhere else. The rides are all outdated (the one new ride didn't even except the fast pass and there was a TWO HOUR WAIT. I was with adults, children and teens and not one of us had a good time. So don't waste yours. We were at the park on Friday, August 21, 2009.

We were there a week ago (7/9/09). This park is ok if you've got young children as lots for them. However Universal could do better at keeping you updated on the rides, as when we were there Terminator & Disaster were not running and no one seemed to give a DAME!! What can we say about Twister!!!!! other than complete rubbish!!!!!!! Staff fairly friendly but not very helpful. Whole place very dated now! Wish we hadn't bothered and save the £110. it cost for the two of us. Go to Animal Kingdom or Seaworld instead, better value for money, by far.

Some of these rides are really feeling their age, they are based on films that I would think most visitors under 20 wouldn't have heard of. My overiding feeling was of being underwhelmed and saying 'was that it??' The newest ride, the RockIt coaster which lets you choose your own soundtrack was a HUGE disappointment! I would definitely not recommend queuing for it. Didn't have time to select a song before it started so got some rubbish techno, the ride was dull and banged my head around a lot. And to top if off the cameras were broken so couldn't see the video of us riding. I'd say skip this park altogether and just go to Islands - the rides there are a million times better! Hulk is my favourite coaster ever.

The attractions inside the park are awesome! Well worth the price of admission! The only thing that went wrong was that a ticket lady persuaded us to add a second park, even though I think she knew there was no way we had time to see it. It cost us $95 to add the Islands of Adventure to our regular park tickets, and we didn't get to see it at all. She told us the park was open plenty late and that we'd get to see it after the Blue Man Group concert, which began at 6PM. Well- she DIDN'T tell us the park closed at 7PM and that the Blue Man Group concert lasted two hours! The guard would not let us back into the park after the Blue Man Group concert was over. We went to "guest services" to get a refund. The shades were all pulled down, but we could see an employee inside moving around. We pounded on the window for a few minutes before she acknowledged our presence. She told us that they DO NOT GIVE REFUNDS, EVEN IF THEIR EMPLOYEE LIED TO US TO SELL US THE TICKETS! She gave us tickets to use at any date in the future (non-expiring tickets) but this was a once-in-a-lifetime trip for us. This bad experience soured me on Universal, and ruined what would otherwise have been a stellar experience.

We went xmas week with our 3 kids, ages 3, 7 and 11. We packed lunches so did not eat in the parks.  The $99 7-day unlimited 2 park deal won us over and we saw almost everything in both parks in 3 days. It was a much better deal than Disney and we had a great time.  For preschoolers, the Barney show is just priceless. If the weather's hot, take a suit for the kids and they can run through the Curious George water play area, which is super fun.  We loved most of the rides, but the Simpsons was the most memorable.

Right off the bat, you get squeezed 12.00 for parking. Tickets into the park(s) were grossly overpriced.  Many of the workers could use some type of training in customer service. We didn't see very many of them smiling, either. A few of them were helpful but the majority seemed unhappy.  Their system of scanning fingerprints and ticket barcodes to enter the park was terribly inefficient.  It rained the day we were there and the leaks were unbelievable. I mean, there were leaks INSIDE several buildings. My kid was next in line to have his picture taken with Sponge Bob in the gift shop - which, of course, was strategically placed at the end of a ride (Jimmy Neutron, I think) - when one of the workers started yelling about a leak. The leak formed a large pool of water on the floor, ending the photo op. There were also leaks - I mean, really big leaks - from overhead coverings when standing in line at several rides. How could that be? It certainly wasn't the first time it ever rained in Florida. Shouldn't Universal have addressed those issues?  The lines weren't long but this was more than likely due to the weather.  The food at Mel's Diner was overpriced. The shakes weren't bad but our burgers were very dry. There were barely enough tables in there to seat all of the people who were eating.  The management of the Men In Black Alien Encounter (or whatever) was extremely poor. As we were getting in line, we were told that all bags had to be stored in small lockers off to the side. This meant getting out of line and walking over to the lockers which didn't have a direct route and was a total mob scene with everyone and their proverbial brother trying to get a locker and narrow walkways. The hold-up was that you are assigned a locker by entering information onto a touch screen. There were two screens that I saw and a mob of people trying to get at them. No workers were around to help or control the scene. No lines. Just a mass of people trying to get to the screens. Plus, part of the deal was that you hadda get your finger scanned. After the ride, it was much of the same. You hadda go to one of the screens and press some buttons to access your locker. To give you a better idea of what a mess this was, after punching in the requested information, a light on your locker goes on which, I guess, helps you locate it quickly. My locker was more than a few feet away from the screen. After I entered my information, the light went on and before I could get to it, some kid saw the light and opened my locker. Now, once the locker is shut you can't get it open. The system "thinks" you removed your belongings. So the girl saw something in the locker and started to shut it and I hadda yell for her to stop before the door closed. What a mess. Oh, and if you don't retrieve your belongings within 45 minutes or so, you have to pay to get your belongings back!  I will say that many of the rides we went on were clever and interesting. This includes Jimmy Neutron, Shrek, Men in Black, Simpsons (which was in the old Back to the Future building, I think), Terminator and Spiderman. ET was so boring that it was painful. And so was the Storm Accelertron (sp?). While on the subject, we thought that many of the Universal rides were blatant knock-offs of Disney rides. ET was like a cross between Peter Pan and Small World; Storm was pretty much the same as the Mad Tea Cup; and Men in Black was like Buzz Lightyear.  I can't imagine us going back again. In fact, the only reason why we went was because my wife got a free ticket as a promotion by Universal during this year's Super Bowl. (Remember the Denny's free breakfast promo?)

After booking this vacation for the sole purpose of seeing Wizard World was very disappointed with Universal Studios. They convinced us to purchase the VIP Express Pass which came to 600 dollars for the two of us. Which suppose to give us fast entry to the rides, attractions, and dinning. Except for the main attraction "Forbidden Journey" ride. As well as one hour early admission. What they failed to tell us that they created a separate long line to get into Wizard World once you got into the park. So the one hour early admission was pointless. We waited hours to get into Wizard World part of the park which made no sense. Once inside there were long lines to everything. Shops, rides and dinning. The Express pass did not get you priority seating for the dinning as they had clearly stated. When we went to Customer Relations, they had no idea about why we couldn't get into Wizard World early. So after they did some checking they told us the pass could not do that. Would of been nice to know this when they were selling it to us. They have excluded Wizard World from the rest of the park, so the same benefits do not apply in this area at all. We expected long lines but not like this. To wait for hours to get into a section of their park was not indicated when you purchase your ticket. People were very frustrated to stand in these unexpected lines in the hot sun just to enter into Wizard World. Universal Studios could have at least gave out free bottle of waters to the guest. They offered no kind of accomodations to their paid guest who came to their park especially to see Wizard World. We are fans who are willing to travel, plan and pay for this attraction. Although Universal Studios seem to care more in getting funds oppose to customer satisfaction. There are hundreds of people complaining about this and I can see why now.

My family stopped en route back from a powerlifting tournament in West Palm Beach. Now, I'll admit that our entire family is larger than normal, but NONE of us has had a problem getting on rides at Disneyworld, Six Flags (Batman ride was close because of my height), or any fairs or festivals.  Because we only had one day, and have never been to Universal, we decided to spend our money there instead of Disney for a change. $345 for a family of four for a one park, one day pass (highway robbery, but Disney was the same price!!).  The kids selected Islands of Adventure because they like the rough rides. Line for Harry Potter was 2-hours as expected in July, but it seemed well organized with a park employee holding a sign to mark the end of the line. The employee also suggested getting in line after 3pm because it is much shorter. They even give you tickets half-way along to indicate any line jumpers.  Our first ride we tried to get on was the River Adventure in Jurassic Park...after 30 minutes of waiting, the ride broke. Nobody could give us an idea of how much longer it would be. Being we were towards the front of the line, we waited another 20 minutes. We asked again how much longer...5 minutes? 30 minutes? 3 hours? Nobody knew. There were no misters to keep everyone cool, so we decided to get out of line. As we were walking out the exit, the ride started back-up (grrrrrrr).  After getting drinks, Harry Potter line was much shorter. Got in line and was in Harry Potter area within 30 minutes. The line is not for a ride per se...it's just to get into the area!! Once you are in, it's a free for all! Lines abounded to poorly labeled rides/shops/etc. First ride we tried to get on was the Dragon Challenge roller coaster. Employee at the entrance said we had to sit in the test seats. Test seats?? Sure enough there were test seats for "Guests with certain body types". NONE of us fit in them...including my 13 year old daughter. Flight of the Griffendorf ride is LAME! The Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey ride had test seats too (no dice). WARNING...there are NO indications on the Universal park maps or on their web site WHICH rides have the test seats. Had we known THIS many rides had them, we could have made a more informed decision about where to spend our money (which is prompting a nasty letter from me to Universal).  Went back to River Adventure in Jurassic Park and it was working (ride #1).  Next tried to ride the Ripsaw Falls water ride in Toon Town. Guess what??? Test seat!! We could get in but you had to put your feet so close to your body that your knees were in your chest!! We decided to wait in line anyway. After an hour of waiting in the extreme heat (misters were not working and line area before going to inside qeue had NO misters and was enclosed so there was no breeze)...guess what BROKEN!!! The employees in the ride were making announcements, but they never turned the music down in the ride...so all you heard was mumbled jibberish. It was only after the third announcement could we make out the phrase "technical problems".  Went to Spider Man ride in the the Super Hero area. Got on the ride, but guess what??? It malfunctioned!! They let us jump back on again and it worked the second time around (ride #2 and 3?)  Test seats on Hulk coaster and Dr Doom Drop (no dice). The kids did get to ride Storm Force Accelatron (wife and I were so mad at this point we didn't want to ride) (ride #4). Both claimed it was lame (Tilt a Whirl at a fair was more exciting).  We had planned to leave at 6:00 anyway due to dinner reservations...so $345 and 8 hours later...we rode 3-4 rides due to time wasted to malfunctioning rides and size limitations.  I will NEVER go to this park again...even at my optimum weight because I would STILL not be able to fit on these rides.

We had a great time at Universal Studios and IOA! The rides at IOA were a blast, lots of coasters and speedy thrills. US was also really fun for its nostalgic rides/attractons and overall vibe.  WWHP was really a site to behold! After reading all of the books and watching all of the movies it was really quite cool to be walking through Hogsmeade and Hogwarts drinking a Hogs Head Ale or frosty Butterbeer.  BUT, they have a lot of work to do with WWHP. It is way too small for the amount of demand there is now and in my opinion will be for a long time. It is crammed at ALL times and feels pretty claustrophobic after an hour or so. I really wouldve liked for them to include some additional streets, like maybe a Diagon Alley area within. Also, There are only 2 rides (one of which is really for young children:flight of the Hippogriff) and theres the Forbidden Journey which is a simulator (beware for those that get nauseous on this type) and not even a ride. THEY NEED MORE RIDES! Great Idea but a lot more needs to be done before the idea becomes a true realization.  Also, City Walk was great times, nightime entertainment was top notch and we generally enjoyed the heck out of what it had to offer.  All in all a great park, but...Cant Be Comapred To The Park That Need Not Be Named!

Those visiting for HHN, be warned. They have teams of security looking for under age drinking and parents who may pass a drink to their kids to hold. Even if your kid is holding the drink for a second, they'll take you to a large processing area, take away your tickets, and ban you for a year. If you argue, you'll be arrested. Many people have been arrested for arguments with security. Do yourself a favor and stay away. The new HP shopping mall has long lines. The new roller coaster is always broke, because it's a carnival coaster.

End of September is a great time to visit Universal. If you start off early when the gates open you can avoid long lines and get a lot more done! I had a great time. The rides were fun and it wasn't too hot to walk around!

We arrived at Universal Studios about 2 hrs. prior to opening on the opening day of The Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Once we were in, we were informed that it would be about 9 hours before we would be allowed to enter that section of the park. I feel that park officials should have been better prepared for the crowds. I saw virtually no one in line to purchase tickets. This means that almost all of the tickets for that day were prepurchased. We did return the next day, and things were much better. Once we got to the main ride, my husband tries the test seat outside the ride and fit. We waited in line for the ride, and when we were almost to the front he tried a second test seat. No problem. As the rest of our family boarded the ride, his seat would not fasten. He is not "Pooh Sized." He is 6'2" and has a tall upper body. I have heard that they have changed the seats, but I would verify it before going again. The ride was amazing! But it was disappointing that we all could not ride.

We visited Universal Studio's Wizarding World of Harry Potter in August 2010...my mom, my 15-year old daughter and myself. The theme park is really fun, but it was also unbelievably crowded. My daughter and I are huge Harry Potter fans and grandma is a fan as well, but not quite as serious.  We stayed at a Universal hotel so we got early access and could skip lines on some of the rides. The early admission and line skipping made the whole day worth it. We got in really early and went straight to the Forbidden Journey ride which we couldn't skip the line on. It was an amazing ride and well worth the short wait that early in the morning. Later in the evening we went back to do it again and wait over two hours!  During the middle of the day when it was most hot and crowded, we went back to our hotel, went swimming and took naps, then went back to the theme park in the evening.  We spent a fortune to have this one day in Harry Potter world, so it's not something I'll do again, but it was really fun.

We went to Universal on Xmas break. Over $600.00 for our group to get in and we spent the whole afternoon to get on one ride. Express tickets, sold out. Priority parking,sold out. Human gridlock, music so loud you had to scream to converse and long lines for everything from bathroom to food. Biggest waste of a day our whole vacation.  Save this attraction for off peak season, if at all!

I'll try to be brief. I feel robbed or at least cheated with our recent visit. It cost over 500.00 and received almost nothing but aggravation. Parking was slow and took at least 20 minutes. Attendants were yelling at guests. We were yelled at to get our stroller off a walk way. We were solicited to buy a credit card. After a long walk we were confronted with another long wait to buy tickets (45 minutes) and more sales attempts (this same process took about 5 minutes at Disney at half the cost). After the hike to Harry Potter we were turned away to go wait in another long line for a timed entrance pass in a very crowed area, also getting yelled at because the whole family was in line not just a representative. (Why this couldn’t be addressed at ticketing or at least the info for the need to get another ticket!) During the day I was only able to go on 3 rides, my family 4. At Disney the hours were always extended due to crowds, at Universal it was the opposite. An employee told us closing was at 8:00 but after assuming there was time to eat (at the worst food in the world, Burger Digs.. We left finding the park closed at 7:00 and unable to do ANYTHING else. At Disney parks we could see characters, shop and linger, nothing at Universal. Harry Potter was somewhat well done but not made for crowds at all, again yelled at for going the wrong way or wrong door. Then the family was subjected to walking thru all the bars and party atmosphere on leaving, not meant for a family. I will never return, I truly feel foolish for throwing away hard earned money to be miserable and feel like I was an inconvience not a guest. If there were a money back guarantee I would be asking for my money back, what a rip off. We left Disney feeling happy with a wonderful experience we left Universal feeling like the only interest was to make money, which of course it is.

Universal Studios is poorly laid out, lacking staff, lacking knowledgeable staff and not a great value. It was confusing, crowded and expensive. The Harry Potter area was visually interesting, but so crowded that there was 45 minute wait just to get into a gift shop. Harry Potter is a separate ticket and you have to stand in a long line to get a ticket and then stand in a line to get into the area, and then stand inline for a ride, food or shopping. It was so crowded there was a two hour wait for the Hogwarts ride and staff said "It was very crowded compared to other days." They definitely over sold the Harry Potter area. If they were truly limiting tickets to certain hours, it was too many people. Good luck in finding first aid, a shady rest spot or anyone to answer a questions.

I went to Universal a few weeks ago and they had some great rides. I loved the Mummy ride, Simpson ride and Spiderman was awesome! We went to Universal Studio's the 2nd day of our trip after Harry Potter. It was nice because it wasnt crowded and the most wait time was15 minutes. I liked the way the rides were set up because as hot as it was outside we stayed cool with most of them being inside or under cover. Even know i liked the Unversal Islands better this was a nice park and i will be back next year!

My family has been to most of them and we all agree that Islands of Adventure rated the worst. We opted for the lower level fast-pass to shorten our wait times, but approx 600 hundred dollars for just the tickets for a family of four - I got ripped off. Most hi-end parks we end up closing the place because there's so much to see & do but here we were done by 4pm.  My teens love fast roller coasters, so deuling dragons and the HULK were fun! But most of the other rides felt outdated. Poseidon looked so cool on the outside! But it comes across as silly inside. Jurassic Park - yawn. Dr. Seuss land was visually stunning, but nothing for teens there. Superhero section was also weak - but we rode HULK multiple times and that was great.  Half my family are Harry Potter fans - so we waited 45 minutes in line JUST TO GET A TICKET TO ENTER Harry Potter village later in the day. When it was our time it was so crowded you could barely get through it - constantly squeezing your way through the crowds. There were 30 minute waiting lines to get into any of the shops. Probably about 15 minute wait for a mug of butter beer. We threw away a couple of hours there and saw next to nothing. The HP ride was ok. I find rides that rely on you watching video screens tend to make me nauseous.  Lunch was another disaster. We waited in a line for over a half hour in the hot sun and only two people walked away with food. Haven't they been doing this a while? Haven't they figured out how to sell product to the masses day in and out? Apparently not. We bailed out of line and grabbed a water and a pretzel at a cart. TIP for those still willing to waste their hard earned money and go: for lunch go back to the entrance because there are more dining options.  Save some money, increase your fun, and go to a Six-Flags - most that I've been to were a lot more fun than this. Disney & Sea World also kick butt on this place.

Universal is far superior to Disney. Lines where not too bad 15-40 mins and directions where plentiful and clear - unlike Disney! Had good time in both parks but Universal ( + adventure land) gets the family vote . Initial pricing seems high but for 10-12 hrs a day it's GREAT VALUE!

I went here with my family 10 years ago and thought it might be an entertaining vacation again....WRONG. The rides are old...the food is dreadful...the shows are also outdated and hokey. Roughly $1000 for two days-parking, lunch,stupid chahka...What was I thinking!!!!?? Spend your dough on a beach vacation in Naples. Orlando is really a boring place

There are a lot of older rides in this half of the Universal--Orlando themepark, but do not miss "The Simpsons ride!" It is a super-fun and thrilling simulated ride and my favorite ride in all of Universal--Orlando! "Revenge of the Mummy" is towards the back of the park, and could be overlooked, but don't! It's a fun roller coaster. The newest coaster in the park is the "Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit;" it's worth a try, but I think it's a very jerky ride, and I only rode it once.
Unless you want to pay through the nose of all the hard earned money you made last month, go. This place is nothing but a shopping mall that charges admission.

The whole experience was overwhelming and as an oldie I did not think that I would enjoy it however I could not have been more wrong. I wished I could have stayed in the park for a week because there was so much to see and do. Harry Potter was exceptional and I will return for a longer period very soon.

I have visited Universal's Islands of Adventure before and love it. I was equally impressed with Universal itself. I do think the rides on this side are more fun. HOWEVER, there is a lot of construction going on so it seemed like a lot of the park was closed or inaccessible. I am looking forward to attending when it is completed.

My family and I went to Universal Studios Orlando on the weekend of Feb 17 and 18. Kelly Clarkston had a concert scheduled in the part at 8 pm on the 18th. That is the exact time the park closes. The crowds quickly formed at the site of the concert. The geniuses at Universal were forcing everyone to go throught the concert site even if all you wanted to do was leave the park. That is all we wanted to do. There was no way that we could make it thru the crowd to leave. We tried to back track to try to go around but the Universal emplyees stopped us and sent us back. I tried to explain that we just wanted to leave and had no desire to see the concert. My young children were overwhelmed by the crowds but the emplyees didn't care. It took us about forty five minutes to get to a restaurant that happened to have two doors. I thought we could cut thru but the crowds jammed the door ways and no one was going anywhere. If there had been a fire or an emergency, there would have been many many people hurt or killed. I even asked one of the emplyees if there was anyone we could call to let us out of the park and she said that I would have to wait until the concert was over. We kept trying and finally back tracked around the entire event not paying attention to anyone that tried to stop us and after an hour and a half finally made it out. I I was planning on getting my kids some souverneirs but by that time the store where we wanted to get them was closed. It was 10:30 pm before we had dinner. Their lack of planning ruined an otherwise good day. It will be a very very long time before I ever return there. This would have never happened at Disney.

This was the second time in two years that we visited Universal Studios in Orlando. We went to "Islands of Adventure" this time around because we wanted to ride the Harry Potter ride we missed two years ago (it wasn't open yet). The park was very clean, well organized, and the mass of people flowed well on a gorgeous Saturday.  Things not to be missed: 1. The highlight of my day was spraying strangers with water while they were riding one of the water rides. They have quarter operated single-shot sprayers that you can use to hose down complete strangers with. My brother and I went through over $50 and laughed the whole time. Yes, they have bill changers next to the sprayers!  2. All of the rides were good. In my opinion (in order from best to least) - The Hulk Roller Coaster, Harry Potter, Sprider Man, The Dragon Roller Coaster, etc...  3. I found the food and drinks to be actually pretty good for park food and actually reasonably priced.  4. They have a dog/cat kennel on site that is great for only $15 for the day.  Things we didn't like: 1. They sell a "Pass the Line" ticket for $50 per person per day. If you purchase this pass you basically can go to the front of any line at any time for the entire day. I'm sure the park is making a lot of money offering this service, but it wasn't much fun to watch people run by us all day long. The longest we waited all day was an hour for Harry Potter. So, I didn't feel like the $100 (for my wife and I) would be worth it.  2. Parking for $15 seemed high to me.  3. If you go to the Universal Studios side of the park - know that there is a maximum height allowed for the rock in roll roller coaster there. I waited for over an hour for that ride two years ago and then was told when I got to the platform that I was too tall to ride. I'm only 6'-5". There are a lot of people much taller than me walking around...
very dated with movie themes that I saw but my kids did not such as terminator, men in black and storm chaser. Not very much to do, not great rides and kids wanted to leave by lunch.

We had a fabulous time at Universal! The longest we waited in line for a ride was 15 minutes for the Spiderman attraction. Most of the time we could walk right up and get on the ride.  Absolutely loved our time at Universal!

Finally was able to afford to go to Universal Studios in Orlando, Florida. Haven’t been there in a very long time. Also, been to your park when it first opened. Made 2 reservations for the park tickets and hotel directly through the Universal Orlando Web Site for 6 of us in total. My wife, 2 nephews, and my in laws. After making the long drive arrived on Monday April 23 until Friday April 27, 2012. Went to Harry Potter World/Islands of Adventures on Tuesday and to Universal Studios on Wednesday. Been wanting to go to your Harry Potter World since it first opened but hasn’t been able to go until now.  To summarize the whole thing, let’s just say that it was a very bad experience and at the end a waste of money. To make things worst, my father in law was on a wheelchair and did not found out until leaving the park on the last day that you offer an “express” pass for people in wheelchairs to make things easier and with assistance. No one said anything about that when we got to the park the first day. Also on your ride at Universal Studios – The Simpsons – had us standing up waiting in the room that you go in before getting on the actual ride for a long time when found out afterwards that could have go in there with the wheelchair and sit and wait.  We also purchased on the first day your meal pass with the drink cups. The food was terrible, cold, and not really worth the money. Was told that the next day will get free drinks since already got the cups and to bring them back. The next day when went to get drinks was told that there was not free and will cost $.80 cents per refill. This shows that was lied about it. Since on the first day the food was horrible and not good, did not purchased the food meal deal the next day.  Also was told that when buying the rides pictures, each picture after the first purchase will be $10.00 each with the photo connect card. That seemed not to be the case when went to get a picture at the Men in Black ride (this wasn’t the first time buying a picture) and was charged the full regular price.  At the end of the second day at Universal Studios went by your guest services department to talk to someone about the entire 2 days bad experience and was told by the guest service representative that was there that had to call a supervisor to talk about of what happened and such. After waiting for 45 minutes no supervisor showed up at all which shows very well that they don’t care at all. Ended up leaving the park.  Also most of the rides that your parks offer now are roller coasters and not meant for the whole family. This makes it not a park for the whole family.  You got rid of the Back to the Future ride and replaced it with The Simpsons. Same type of ride but different “theme”. That does not makes it new, and by the way the Back to the Future ride was much better. You also get rid of Jaws and is closed and nothing there, also seems to be in the process of building a ride for Dispicable Me and Sponge Bob. Your Terminator 3D you seemed to have cut the “show” in half and got rid of a lot of it. We are all very unhappy and dissatisfied with our visit. What it was supposed to be a fun vacation it wasn’t.  For what it cost in total going to your theme parks would have gone to somewhere else like Disney and I bet it would have been much better.  I will tell everyone I know about my terrible experience with you and to beware and consider not going and go somewhere else.  The only reason ended up going to Island of Adventures is because that is where Harry Potter World is and no other way of going to it without going to Island of Adventures.  Universal it is NOT what it used to be when started, that is for sure. Going down the drain !

Universal Studios, as in the park has became very poor. Most of the rides are alright ( The Mummy is probably my favorite of them all ) this park is just a collection of rides, no real theme or connection between them. The parks one real bit of theming which is the Streets, has been ruined by the building of the Rockit rollercoaster ( see picture ). If you want just rides then it wouldn't be an issue, but if you had to chose between here and Islands of Adventure then its no contest in both theme and rides.
Great way to spend a day if you are a movie buff... Awesome Rides!!!

Our flight was in by 830 am and we were at Universal Studios by 10 am....after renting a car! Celebrating Mardi Gras......easy parking,.....long walk in tho...but we were so excited it didnt matter.....Was an excellent day....visited just about all the attractions we wanted to.....just one complaint.....we were there from the airport and I had my handbag and wasnt admitted to an attraction...had to put it in a locker that was outside the attraction.....I was not comfortable with leaving my bag with all my credit cards and cash out there so we did not go on the ride. We stayed all day and nite for the parade and concert with Cyndi Lauper! Perfect first day in Orlando with my teenager son! We will be coming back in July with both my sons!

Went on May with 4 teenagers -- had a blast. our time was limited so we scheduled well the rides to hit 2 parks ( Islands of Adventure and the regular Universal) in one day. It was doable bec the place is compact (unlike Disney). Saved money and time. Most favorite ride is The Harry Potter one and all the wet rides... There are free lockers to store belongings -- leave huge bags home/hotel bec they will not fit. When hungry and tired after the whole day of gallivanting? No worries -- a lot of restaurants to choose from in the Universal City walk. Parking is covered building -- NICE !!!

I had high expectations, me, my husband and 10 yr old son. There wasn't much to do in there. The day we went, we walked on to everything, no lines, and we even had fast passes and didn't need them. I thought it was old, and outdated. The ET ride is OLD! The Jaws ride is gone, and that whole area is under construction. The MIB ride....kinda lame....Disaster...ugh, kind of a disaster. Twister....o.k. kind of lame. Shrek was fun, and that was about it. We got pix with the characters there, that was okay. We saw everything and left the park at 3:00pm. I won't go back there, I would rather go to something else. Local news reported 2 price hikes in a month on tickets and people were screaming about it. The bathrooms were shut down twice for flooding...This place in't worth the money.

There are 3 separate areas, first you walk through the restaurants and bars, then choose to go right to Universal Studios where the rides are based on 10-20 year old movies--or--you turn left to the Islands of Adventure where you can see Harry Potter, Spiderman and several roller coasters to jumble your tummy. Much different than Disney, but quite worthwhile.
This is by far the best Halloween event in the country. We return every year and even went for our honeymoon.

We bought two day tickets in advance. My wife did not feel well after the first day and I took a night flight from New York to go with kids to the park on the next day. When I arrived I was told that the tickets are not refundable or transferrable. Even more: Susan, the guest services lady told me in a 'harsh and cold' voice that I should not be bothering her but rather go with my child to the common line (about hour long) to buy a brand new ticket. I have three question: 1. Why tickets are not refundable or transferrable? I would understand that if we would talk about French or US Open tickets because it helps to avoid speculation. 2. Why the tickets lines that long? 3. Why people like Susan work with customers?  I personally do not plan to return to this park any time soon.

good day had here, this side of Universal has a slower pace to it with more shows, however the big roller coaster is a must for thrill seekers.... Dispicable me is a must do for all ages, absoluetly brilliant

I have taken my family to Universal Studios every year since 1997. After the blatant political bias that was evident during the HHN Bill and Ted show, I will never be back. This was supposed to be family entertainment not a ridiculously obvious infomercial supporting Obama!! Never again will I spend money here!

Why after 10 months would Universal Studios or GE not respond to my concern about our visit last year. Just to reiterate, they've turned this them park into a long wait, hard sell and very annoying experience. We were about 20th in line when the ticket windows opened and waited an HOUR to get in. Every ticket seller was trying to upsell and customers were at the windows for 15 - 30 minutes. This is ridiculous and wasteful. When I asked to speak to a manager I was denied. When I asked for a name to contact I was denied. I'm sick of large companies that are perfectly comfortable trampling on customers rights. If hat wasn't bad enough when we got in the trash barrles were overflowing with trash with garbage and cups on the ground. I think it would be good training for all Universal employees to spend a morning at Disney World. Fix this GE or at least respond to me!! Ronp7214aol.com

If your kids are over 9 this is the park for you. Lots of thrill rides and shows. It is the best theme park in Orlando hands down. I was a Disney nut for years until a friend told me to try Universal and now I am hooked. Last week we spent 4 days in Disney a 4 in Universal and regret the 4 in Disney. Lots of Great places to eat in City walk with no need to get on a Bus. Don't miss the mini golf either.

Universal studios was great but please realize it is more shows than rides, We brought along a 3 year old and she could not do a good amount of the activities. I recommend 5 and older for this park. If choosing between universal and islands of adventure, i would go to islands of adventure because that has more rides as well as harry potter world. Nonetheless, all the shows and rides are amazing. A few of the best are the horror makeup show, revenge of the mummy. ET adventure, woody woodpecker's nuthouse coaster, fear factor live, and the simpson's ride.

visited jan 2012,was staying in disney port orleans resort.I had 2 park tickets, took a cab ride there and back from disney, cost $68 return plus tip.We had an early start, and stayed all day, entry queues were fairly long, but ticketing was simple, we bought neck pass holders for $3 each to store tickets in,good move..This is a looong day, especially doing both parks,too much to take in really, queues were minimal,probs 10 to 15 mins wait on most rides, this is the place to come if you like rides,in the end we ran out of time,i travelled with a 9 yr old and a 16 yr old, they loved the rides.Harry potter world is brilliant, we bought wands to bring home, queues for ollivanders were ridiculous, so skipped that,butter beer was lovely.I found the walk into the park neverending,and because of this and the cab fare, didn't go back, even though our tickets lasted 2 weeks.It was no cheaper to get an organized coach, and travelling solo, i would not use another transport.There were a LOT of teens in these parks,a lot of running around excited kids,not really the family atmosphere you get in the disney parks.I'm going back to disney this year, i have not bought tickets for universal this time, so overall,a very expensive, but totally amazing day out!

Please bear in mind we are a couple in our 30's with no children and Universal had been recommended to us as a place for people of all ages.  We visited Magic Kingdom and hated it. We visited Epcot and thought it was great and we visited Disney Hollywood Studios and it wasn't quite as good as Epcot. We really did think that the Magic Kingdom was poor until we visited Universal Studios. Then we realised it was poor but not the worst and most over-rated place.  Things started off badly at Universal. We had already got the tickets at Seaworld the day before (A 14 day Orlando Flex Ticket for admission to multiple parks). We queued up in the long queue at the gates only to be told that our tickets were not valid because we got them from Seaworld and it's Spring Break. I was quite annoyed because I wouldn't purchase tickets for 14 days if I knew they weren't valid by the next day. I went to Guest Relations and queued up again and they said there was nothing wrong with them. Queued up again at the gates with a different person and got in straight away.  We were expecting Universal studios to be about shows because the next door Islands of Adventure was about rides. However there was some nice themed streets but overall it was just more rides but indoors rather than outdoors. We expected to be able to see how they produced the movies and see some informational shows. The only real show was a show called Fear which was a live show with real visitors, but we only watched it for about 10 minutes before getting bored and leaving. Instead Universal studios was just a series of buildings with themed rides based on old movies. It was rather boring. The only benefit was really the surrounding area of Universal Citywalk which was a very well laid out area with plenty of restaurants, cinema, crazy golf and shops to choose from.

Only one good thing to say about our family visit. The ribs were good. That is it! This park is expensive, over crowded, has rude employees. Now, I know it was spring break, not the best time to go if you don't like crowds, but this was impossible. One of our first experience with the park staff, was when we waited 15 minutes for the man to scan in our tickets to enter the park, and the machine would not work...he said "go to the Back of the line" and walked away WHAT? Waited over two hours for the Spiderman ride~ Loud music playing while we were waiting~Could go on about all of this, but read other reviews~ I guess they don't care much for our, the customers experience.........they are just in it to get as much $$ as possible out of your pocket. Also, to get the line cut pass where you can go to the front of the line, just pay $100.00 per person~ talk about creating a negative class system. Again, I know it was spring break, but to treat customers like this is appalling! Also, just wanted to add, I went to another large sea mammal park the next day and even with the crowds, I was very impressed with how they still were able to create an awesome experience. Just Saying!!!

I don't even know where to begin. We started at Universal Studios on our holiday, they have a wide selection of rides for all ages, and are constructing new ones at the moment. The Simpsons Ride is a fantastic family ride, along with Men In Black: Alien Attack and Despicable Me: Minion Mayhem, however my favorite ride in the parks (and all of Florida) is the Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit, it looks a lot worse than it actually is and you shouldn't miss it out. it's a rollercoaster where you choose a song to listen to, which is synced perfectly to the ride, and I find it fantastic. We also went for the Mardi Gras parade which was a great event, and watched the "Universal Nighttime Spectacular" in the lagoon afterwards.  Next Up, Islands of Adventure, this park is generally busier than Universal Studios due to The Wizarding World of Harry Potter, however shouldn't be missed. My advice is leave Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey right until the end of the day, when I went the wait time was 125 minutes in the morning, and went down to 20 around 9pm. I usually start the day by heading over to Superhero Island, which features the Incredible Hulk Coaster, another fantastic ride, one of my favorites, there's also other attractions and "The Amazing Adventures of Spiderman" which was recently refurbished into HD 3D, and is a half virtual half track ride, in which you follow Spiderman around the streets of Manhattan. As you continue, you'll enter Toon Lagoon, the 2 main rides are Dudley Do Right's Ripsaw Falls and Popeye and Bluto's Bilgerat Barges, Log Flume and Rapids rides. Nothing Special. Through the Jurassic Park area, you'll come into The Wizarding World of Harry Potter. The Butterbeer always has long lines, but is worth it, it's also nice to look around the shops as well. The Dragon Challenge coaster (Formerley Dueling Dragons) Usually has a wait of <20 minutes, as most of the crowd goes to Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey.  Universal Orlando resort host's my favorite parks in Florida, and my favorite coaster in the world. If you have teenagers, this is a MUST SEE. Do not miss out!

We must have spent over 10 hours in the park, riding every ride at least twice, and each of the roller coasters 6 times!! The Minion Mayhem ride is great too, but had the largest lineup in the park. Near the end of the day someone leaving the park gave us their express passes, and I can't explain how much they help. I would consider buying them next time we go. You get to skip all the lines!!

What a hackneyed word, but the only one which really describes this experience. I thought this was superior to Disney, but was influenced by the fantastic job they did with recreating a realistic Harry Potter experience. Bearing in mind that my wife and I are in our mid 60's, and was accompanied by my daughter & husband, and their two children, all of whom had an even better time than us!!! Initially I had some reservations when I discovered how expensive it was, but in retrospect, it was money well spent. We had a two day ticket, which I would suggest you need as a minimum, in order to enjoy the many facilities available. Average wait was circa 15 to 20 minutes per ride, with some of the more popular stretching to 30 mins. I would rate 'Harry Potter Land' as currently the major attraction available.

Universal is more for kids 8-16 years of age. It is a down-sized Disney. Most of the rides were simulated and involved 3D Glasses. Each park had one coaster. Universal Studio was better than islands of Adventure. We purchased the food ticket and drink ticket. We had no trouble finding the restaurants and drinking refills at Universal but Islands was hard to find and scarce drinking refills. The Maps for each park are really crummy - they definetely need more details to help you find places or find yourself! Signage is not helpful. Going into Islands - the music is way too loud; hasn't the Park realized we are teaching our kids to turn down the volume to save their hearing. Most of the attractions were a lesser copy of a Disney Ride. Not enough attractions. Shops were a bit high priced. Food was good at the Universal Restaurants on the Meal ticket.

For my very first Universal trip, I really enjoyed the original park. We did not buy the express pass and we only waited for one ride. I enjoy the fact that Universal goes out of their way to make their guests comfortable, far exceeding what I've seen at Disney and Six Flags. Air conditioning, big fans, and quick lines are awesome!

Gutted! Out of all the parks we had done as a family we were looking forward to this park. We paid for the tickets beforehand luckily as queues were long. Entered the park early (0830). We were at the Island Adventures side. Baring in mind tickets are expensive we were shocked at the queues already in place, especially for Harry Potter 'rides' location. If you choose to fast pass this park it is called 'express pass'. A further $96 per ticket.(Disney Fast Pass included in price) Although we done most the rides the park is not as enjoyable as Disney attractions and we believe unless a mass Harry Potter fan it can be avoided.

the thing about universal studios that is better than disney is the lines are not that long and the attractions are much closer together than at disney. you could see everything in one day if weather permits, where as disney is so spread out you could spend days and never see everything. my teen actually prefers universal over disney

Recently went to Orlando Studios, Adventure Land, Orlando, Florida & had a very good time. Liked the rides, shops, magic show, etc there. Didn't even have enough time to take it all in on one day so plan to return there in the future! Offered a variety of different rides for all family members & loved the Harry Potter castle & ride!
My eight year old, husband and I had great time. Harry Potter Island of adventure was fantastic. Transformers ride highly recommended

I go to Universal probably 5 times a year because I have an annual pass. We just went for the first time without an express pass and the lines were too long. I love Universal but the lines were too long. So here are some steps to having a great time at Universal.  1. Dont stay 1 day  If you are going to Universal Studios do NOT only stay one day. There are 2 parks and so much to do.  2. Stay in one of the on-site hotels  If you stay in one of the on-site hotels, you get the advantage of getting a unlimited express pass. What that means is that you can go on a ride more than once with this express pass. The one you buy in the park can only get you on that ride once.  3. Buy a souveneir cup  When you buy a souvenir cup you get 79 cent refills. Less money = Why not?

Not as fun as Universal Islands of Adventure for a family with high school kids but had some good points. Lombard's Seafood restaurant was really good. I don't care for the Simpsons so there was ALOT too much of that for me. Also the only employees on the entire Universal vacation we encountered who were bad were at Ben & Jerrys in the Park. 3-4 people working and only one of them trying. The rest trying to close the place at 5:40 and didn't care about the line backing up out the door  Everything else was really good but not as good as Islands of Adventure.
Went as an add-on to Islands of Adventure. New Transformers ride was awesome. The Mummy never disappoints. Food was good. Overall a worth getting the park-to-park pass.
A great day out at the film studios where the rides are based on famous movies. Thoroughly enjoyed the visits we have made here. An adventurous day to say the least.

Each visit to Universal is a new experience as more attractions are added year on year. Latest rides are always extremely busy, but that means older ones are quieter .. MIB, Simpsons, Terminator 4D, Shrek and Twister were all walk ins, whereas a few years ago the lines were huge. Next year the Harry Potter experience moves in to Universal and this will again take pressure off the new rides .. Transformers and Despicable me.. A very full day .. or two .. lol.

Expensive tickets, long lines, only one good venue. Transformers 3D. All others were terrible. The meal tickets and drink tickets weren't worth the price. Meal tickets only good at three locations and drinks at five. All fast food that wasn't tasteful. An additional $16 to park. What a ripoff!!

Harry Potter world is unbelievable. The rides are INSANE! The food at the Three Broomsticks is fabulous! We had dinner, The Feast, which was salad, corn on cob, fresh steamed veggies, roasted potatoes, grilled chicken and ribs. Oh, and some butter beer. YUMMY! Don't miss this park if you visit Orlando.

Vegans please be aware that Universal Studios lies about food to get you to go there. 4 times Bob Burdick, chef at Universal Studios, Orlando told me that all the cheese on pizzas is vegan. On my 5th message to him I checked if he knew what a vegan was and explained it to him, highlighting that I believe the cheese had cows milk in it. Bob Burdick then admitted that the cheese was not vegan at all and blamed it on his suppliers giving him the wrong information I complained about Bob to customer services and several days later I received a phone message from customer services stating that they had spoken with Bob Burdick and all the cheese is vegan. Doh!!! It clearly is not. Why is he lying about this to people? He has admitted to me it is not vegan but is continuing to tell people that it is vegan. I wouldn't not expect all the cheese to be vegan and that is not what I am asking - Just be honest, as you could make people with milk allergies really ill....

I have been to universal studios the past three years and I just can't get enough of it! It is a wonderful holiday experience with lots to do. All the rides are based on movies which is great because it makes you feel like you are in the movie. Both parks are really clean and the staff are really friendly. The restaurants are nice and the food is delicious! I would highly recommend the Hard Rock Cafe and the three broomsticks at the wizarding world. I would recommend not going in the summer season because it can get really busy and the queues get really long. So going out of season would be more beneficial. Although the parking is expensive at $16, it's still good as it's all uncover and is linked to the parks with walkways so you don't have to walk far. The parks are well sign posted and maps are provided in order to get around easily. I love this place and I'm going again next year!!!!
Most kids don't know what ET is....needs to be removed and another ride put in it's place. It is slow loading and just not worth the wait.

they have several food choices that were amazing to eat at. The ride waits we not that bad plus if it was a specific ride to a certain movie then while you are waiting they would have things you can look at or even watch while you are waiting.

We went to Islands of Adventure on Dec 28th, 2013. We have never felt so ripped off in our lives from start to finish. First off, we had to wait in line for 40 mins to park. We were then charged $16 to park. We paid almost $100 each for 5 entry tickets. Upon entering the park, it started to rain, which granted, we were not prepared for. We duly had to pay $8 each for plastic bags to cover ourselves, $40 total. Universal is likely buying these bags for about 2 cents each. They could easily make them complimentary to their patrons. The average wait time for the majority of the major rides was an hour and a half, and 2 hours for Harry Potter. We felt compelled to purchase 2 express passes at a mind boggling cost of $139 each!!!! Even with these passes, we found we could not use them for the Harry Potter Forbidden Journey. When we got wet on some of the water rides, we decided to use the drying facility at a cost of $5 per use! Again, this could easily be complimentary or at worst $1. It just seemed that they shamelessly wanted to screw customers out of every last dime. Toon land is a complete joke. Incredible Hulk, Jurassic park and Spider-Man are good rides. Seuss land is great for smaller kids. We left the park at 9pm after having spent close to $1,000 and we brought our own food!!! We will not be back and we will be recommending that none of our friends go there. Disney is so much more customer friendly and organized, with knowledgeable staff. It is altogether much more worthwhile with a speed pass system that is fair to all, not just the few who can afford to fork out exorbitant fees for express passes.

We went to Universal for the first time at the end of December 2013 and beginning of January 2014. All of the Christmas decorations were still in place and I must admit they do a lovely job of decorating. That being said - THE WAIT TIMES FOR RIDES ARE HORRENDOUS!! Over 2 hours for Despicable Me/Minions and Harry Potter! Why does Universal NOT GET A CLUE?? When you trap people in lines for rides, they are NOT SPENDING $$ ON THEIR OVER PRICED FOOD AND SOUVENIERS!! Charging people for an "Express pass" isn't going to work - people will almost always choose to wait over shelling out more money to ride an attraction. Be smart Universal and copy the FREE Disney fast pass system so you can squeeze more $$ out of the guests!!

I had heard so much about this event that my boyfriend and I decided to go to it instead of Howl O Scream ( won't make that mistake again). The line for every house was no less than 100 mins and that was with the fast pass. We only got to 4 of the 8 houses. There were more booze stands than anything else and the place was full of drunk people that at one stage you could not tell the difference between them and the staff dressed as zombies. The only saving grace was the Rocky Horror Tribute which was FANTASTIC. I love Universal Studios but this is one event I won't be returning for.

We visited on Feb 15. The equipment kept breaking down and the lines take forever. They told us transformer line was 45 min. But after 3 hours they finally said the ride was having mechanical issues. We had made it to the ride but couldn't wait any longer.

Universal Studio Parks in Orlando are Exceptional. We have been to Universal Studio in Hollywood which is excellent but the Orlando Parks cannot be beaten for the rides, shows and especially the Harry Potter Theme and rides. Bush Gardens have some hair raising roller coasters too and is a brilliant day out. Discovery Cove and Aquatica are high up on our list plus all the numberous dinner shows e.g. Pirates, Sleuths, Magic Show which are all on I-drive

i'm not into thrill rides but these appear to be the main (only?) strengths of this park. live entertainment was lame, parade canceled as soon as it started. food poor and pricey. less crowded than Disney, for a reason.

It does feel like many rides here are getting old.  I suspect the new Harry Potter themed area will give it a big lift.  Still worth a visit, but seems to have faded compared to it's sister park right next door!

I have been going to Universal regularly for several years and one thing I can count on is that there will always be some sort of construction going on at the park. I really enjoy the park overall and love the Springfield area but only appreciate coming here because I have an annual pass that makes it a good value.  I don't think it's worth the price of a 1 day ticket. Many rides like Simpsons and Transformers are great. I just watched the Beetlejuice show for the first time and was actually impressed at how good it was but they lack the attention to detail that Disney gives to the appearance of their parks. The streets just look dirty and old. A lot of the buildings have giant printed tarp coverings on them, I don't know why.  The quality of the staff has been declining over the years also, I guess that they don't emphasized friendliness in training and evaluations anymore.  Overall I still enjoy going and liked that the lines were reasonable when I went without needing an Express Pass but I hope that management takes a break from building new things after the Harry Potter section opens to improve the visual appearance of the rest of the park.

I absolutely loved both Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure. Definitely my favorite park over Disney world. Visited multiple times over a two week period and enjoyed every second of it. I have never been a big theme park rider, I'd usually be the bag holder but universal changed my mind. My favourite rides where the Harry Potter and the forbidden journey which was AMAZING and the equally amazing Transformers ride.  Stay for the fireworks and pyrotechnics show at the end of the day, this is an amazing showcase of movies with special effects. And if you love Pizza, why not check out Red Oven Pizza in City Walk. Quick and delicious!  The staff where friendly, the merchandise well priced and the facilities clean. I would return in the future, maybe to experience the new harry potter exhibit that is being opened this Tuesday.  I would recommend a multiple day pass, it can be very tiring and is quite nice to come back on multiple times both evening day. Also choose preferred parking if you do not want to walk a long way to get to the attractions.  Overall a thoroughly enjoyable experience and a highlight of my holiday.

Universal Studios is awesome. Had a great time. Rides for all ages. Wait time was not bad. New Harry Potter ride was incredible. If you are a Harry Potter fan you must go to Diagon Alley - it was awesome.

I enjoyed my third visit to Universal Studios en Orlando, however I do not think I will go back because there is so much to see and do that I was too exhausted in the evening. It seems I am getting old! I made the mistake of purchasing entrance for two parks, and I hardly was able to enjoy just one. I would recommend to purchase at least two-days entrance, otherwise you will not have time to do what you paid for. Please take the best walking shoes you have, sun protection hat/umbrella, and cream. If you do not want to wait too long for a ride just go single. It is a great decision. Have fun!

The hype for The Harry Potter attractions at Universal was huge so we were on a mission to see what all the fuss was about. We got to the park at 7am and went straight to Diagon alley. Thinking we were ahead of the queue we were told by the attendants we had a 2 hour wait... To our horror 2 hours turned into 4, the lines seemed to move quickly to start but the ride kept breaking down so we were left sitting on hard floors for up to 45 mins at a time. It was utterly utterly awful. People were treated like herded cattle , no information or updates on what was going on, and because you cannot see how long the queue is, you keep in the line. There was no option for express passes on any of the new Potter attractions only the old re purposed roller coasters . Whilst the attraction itself was good, the awful queue experience completed negated any positive memory . It really is an awful awful way to treat people and completely ruined the Universal theme park experience for us. If you have 4-5 hours of your life to waste sitting in searing heat for an approx 7 min ride go for it. It's bad enough for adults but even worse for poor kids...For die hard Potter fans the ambience and attention to detail in Diagon alley may be worth it for you. I certainly would not recommend it to anyone else . The rest of the universal rides were awesome in particular the Mummy, Spider-Man and Despicable me , however the morning experience really ruined our day. Sort yourselves out Universal, do not bring these poor unsuspecting tourists on the promise of great things to your attractions that break down constantly and make people wait 4 hours in Florida heat... It's utterly dispespectful and a complete con!

Overall good experience. The downfall was the time to wait in line.. The Minion ride was 3 hours at one point. You don't have time to visit both parks in one day. But it was fun and the whole family enjoyed. The Simpson's ride was awesome! Transformers was pretty great too!!!

We've visited both parks in 3 days, and had time to make all the attractions, some of them more than once. 3-day ticket is a good deal, but remember you must choose the park hopper option to visit more than one park a day. If you didn't choose this option, you won't be able to take the Harry Potter's train that links both parks!

We could not understand how people could spend a full day here unless they stood in a long queue for every ride. Mostly just shops and overcrowded places to eat which we thought were overpriced. Certainly not worth the entrance fee.

Universal Studios (and Islands of Adventure) are much better than the Disney Parks, from the ease of parking and being able to walk into the parks, the proximity of City Walk, the on site restaurants being a million times better than those in Magic Kingdom or Hollywood Studios, the way the park is organised with very little "dead" space between attractions, Universal has done it right, but it could be much better.  Why they don't offer fast pass tickets on the big Harry Potter rides is a mystery, making people queue for upwards of 3 hours to get on the Escape from Gringotts ride must be a lost revenue opportunity for them, and be aware that Diagon Alley and Escape from Gringotts get stupidly busy.  Universal offer an hours access before official opening hours for resort hotel guests, so even if you get there at 8am for general admission and speed walk to Diagon Alley you'll find a 30 minute queue just to get into the Alley and another 3 to 4 hour queue for Escape from Gringotts.  We had a shockingly bad experience on our first visit, where we arrived at the park for 8am, entered the Gringotts queue at 8:05am and it was supposed to be 150 minutes, after 4 hours we were still about 30 minutes (estimated) from getting on the ride when they announced that the ride was temporarily closed due to technical difficulties and wouldn't reopen for at least 45 minutes. So we left, picking up complimentary Express Pass tickets for the ride as compensation. After some googling I found out this happens every day! The ride is so advanced and cutting edge that when something goes wrong, they pretty much have to reboots the whole system, and it takes 20 minutes to do that!  So we went for lunch came back and used the Express Pass tickets to get to just before where we'd been when we bailed. It still took c 45 mins to get on the ride from there, because everyone else who'd done the same was using their free passes.  The queue once you get inside the bank is good, the main hall with the goblins is great, the tunnels quite good and the show with the goblin and the Weasley is good. The ride itself is awesome, clearly not worth 4 hours queuing up for (nothing is) but is just about as immerssive into Harry Potter that you can get, and is marginally better than Forbidden Journey (but the queue is not as good) because Gringotts is in 3D so when Nagini attacks....you jump! A lot.  The rest of Diagon Alley is well done, the little wizarding points for those who buy the interactive wands are great and very interesting. Borgin and Burkes and Ollivanders are ace. The Leaky Cauldron is good also. Watch out for fire from the Dragon atop Gringotts.  Outside Diagin Alley you'll find the Knight Bus complete with Stan Shunpike - go and talk to him because the rasta head talks to you and is clearly voiced by someone who can see you as it will interact with you about your clothes and call you by your name. There is the Order of the Phoenix House, and a few other things.  Kings Cross Station is well done and the visual effect of walking through the wall at 9 3/4 is great. Hogwarts to Hogsmeade is brilliant, watch out for Dementors! The journey each way is different, so make sure you do both if you have duel park tickets (which as a Potter fan you must get).  Away from Potter other good things in Universal Studios we went on:  Rip Ride Rocket Rollercoaster - great, worth a 45 min queue The Simpson Ride - good, wouldn't queue for more than 30 mins for Men in Black - average - 15 mins queue max ET - old and weak - 10 mins Revenge of the Mummy - scary, our 8 year old son screamed! worth 45 min queue Minion Mayhem - Funny and good, huge queues though, not worth more than 45 mins Shrek 4D - OK - 20 mins max Beetlejuice Graveyard Revue - poor - don't bother.  We ate at Lombards Seafood Grille which is a proper table service restaurant and very good!  One negative note, we had reason to complain, as we'd been told we could get access to the park from 7am from 1st Aug, so we could get into queue for Escape from Gringotts early as some compensation for the 5 hour wait we had on the first time, so after complaining at Guest Services (and getting the brush off) I emailed Universal. After some toing and froing I was offered some Express Passes for another visit, and upon collecting then was told they were NOT valid on Harry Potter rides (FJ and EfG) despite the telephone conversation the previous day not mentioning this at all, which was rather annoying considering the issue arose due to a fault with EfG. Guest Services couldn't help me further so I had to wait half an hour and ring customer services again, I was then told that she "would make an exception and do me a favour by allowing me to swap two of my Express Passes for ones that would work on EfG" I was not happy at now having to go back to Guest Services and at the fact that she said she was doing me a favour, so I asked to speak to a manager in Guest Services and Corey did the right thing and gave us Express Passes for both of the big Potter rides.
