Took 3 emails, 3 telephone conversations and 3 face to face conversations to finally get someone who delivered good service!

I'm 22 and the last time I was at universal studios I was 10. Went there and did almost every ride. Only rockit was closed due to the weather. I did not have express passes but went into single riders line everywhere it was available. My favorites were the Transformers and the Mummy. Choose less crowded days or ue single riders line to save the money of express passes.

We queued for far too long! It broke down 5 times while we were queuing. The ride it self was a very poor relation to the ride in the other park. It last 3 minutes and didn't thrill or excite, so when asked if we wanted to queue again on the fast track our group voted with its feet and went back to the other Harry Potter ride in the other park!

I have never been to a visitor attraction where every member of staff has no interest in visitors offering zero customer service. How can you queue for 4 hours to go on a Harry Potter ride in the 90 degree sun and not see a single member of staff . On arrival we were told that both parks closed at 6 pm for a private function. We checked with two other staff who confirmed they had just been told that both parks closed at 6. Then at 6 having changed plans we found out only one park closed at 6.All staff appear totally disinterested and any question asked appears to be a major inconvenience to them . Universal have a lot of lessons to learn from Disney

We visited Universal Studios in July 2014 with designs on riding the new Escape from Gringotts attraction; arriving before the gates opened to be near the front of the line. It took 15 minutes to walk to Diagon Alley and even though there were only a couple of hundred people walking with along with us, the wait was already 90 minutes. Once we turned the corner and could see the rear of the line it was apparent that Universal doesn't know how to estimate time. There were over 2,000 other guests already in line! After 5 breakdowns and 4 hours in line, we finally gave up. The ride was clearly not ready to handle non-stop use but instead of closing it and making repairs, they just "fixed it as it went" and hoped people didn't complain. Wrong! Unfortunately, there was no ride manager with whom we could share our anger. For over an hour we were stuck inside the dark bank vault and none of the attendants offered any explanation for the delays or assistance to those who were suffering from the cramped quarters. A bottle of water would have been a welcomed sight. Having 3 backpacks in our group, we asked before entering if they were permissible on the ride and were told to keep them and half way through, someone would hold them for us; NOT! Before being permitted to enter the lower level of the bank, we were stopped and told that backpacks aren't allowed and we would have to put them in lockers - which are outside! So while four members stepped out of line and waited, I secured the bags. The lockers are fingerprint access and although it didn't seem like an issue at the time when someone needed something important from her purse 90 minutes later, I was the only one who could retrieve it! Again, no one on the Universal Team had any compassion for the problem. When we found our way out of the Alley, the next ride (Disaster) was also broken down but at least they had the decency to bar people from getting in line. By now it was after 1:00 so we broke for lunch. Note, we'd been in the park for 5 hours and hadn't ridden any rides! After our food, two of us decided to try our luck on the Rip Ride Rocket. The rest of the group sat and waited because the line was only 45 minutes long. When we hadn't returned 90 minutes later they came looking for us. The cause for the delay? We got stranded on the track and had to be rescued. This was no fun either. It was pushing 4 pm and we still hadn't successfully completed a ride so we marched to the customer service office. The representative didn't appreciate our incredible disappointment of being at her park for 8 hours and all we did was stand in lines and give them money for food. We wanted our money back but that was out of the question. Even letting her know that "the internet is a powerful tool for rating attractions" didn't sway her. The level of customer service at Universal is beyond terrible and I would not recommend the park to anyone. No one cares if you're happy or sad, they're just glad to have your cash. Three teenagers got to see the Wizarding World of Harry Potter but at $70 per person, it was a huge waste of money.

Universal studios has something for all ages. This is my family's favorite theme park. The new rides like Tansformers,The minion ride and the Simpsons ride were awesome. The workers there are so wonderful. My daughter's asthma got really bad due to the heat and we took her to the first aid office to check her vitals. They checked her out and got us a special pass so that she could skip,the lines.we were just going to leave because we were concerned about her being out in that heat and humidity. The heat was agrivating her asthma. I was very happy that they have such a kind staff.

Arrived at with great excitement at Universal at 8.30am. Battled our way through the security, crowds and finally got into the park at 9am and headed towards Harry Potter. The Despicable Me ride had already got a queue for 80 minutes which was hard to believe since the park had only opened at 9am! We decided to buy Express Passes at $70 each totally $300 with tax for 4 people and headed to Diagon Alley. The Gringotts ride had a 4 hour wait by 9.30am and we were then informed that our Express Passes where not valid on Harry Potter rides!! We abandoned Gringotts and looked around Diagon Alley which was excellent! You are able to visit inside the shops which was magical and better than the Warner a Brothers Studios in the UK! We then headed to the Kings Cross station which was a very good replica of the real thing with the destination board showing departures on my local line which was very amusing to my daughter! We went onto Platform 9 3/4 and magically disappeared onto the other side! Great for all Harry Potter fans! The Hogwarts steam train is fantastic where you travel to the a Islands of Adventure with Harry and crew passing past the window. On arrival you are faced with Hogwarts castle in the snow and yes yet more queues which my Express passes are not usable! We spilt up and my husband went the castle ride and queued for 80 minutes and I went with my other daughter into the Wand shop to see the magic demonstration which took 1 hour in the burning sun! We decided against buying any Butter Beer as we had sampled it at the Studios! We returned back to Universal travelling back on the Hogwarts express and made our way to Disaster! By now it was 11.30am and even paying $300 we had only been on 1 ride and the train. We used the a Express Pass and went in with the normal queue still waiting 30 minutes to use the ride! By 1pm we attempted to go on Despicable Me and again waited 40 minutes with the Express Passes so at 2.30 we had managed 2 rides which had cost $300. My husband went to guests services who eventually got a full refund of $300. We then managed to meet Curious George, Shaggy and Scooby Doo, Dora and Sponge Bob and went on the ET ride and Shrek by 5pm and exhausted we left the park feeling very let down! We did not have time to eat a meal at Universal due to all the time queuing. I think Universal could learn by the success on the Disney FastPass+ which are free!
Again like islands of adventure highly recommend fast @ $88 each. Would have only done 3 rides if no passes as the queues were quite long.

Like Islands of adventure, we had so much fun at the universal studios! Harry Potter comes out on top, the diagon alley is sensational and the gringotts rode fantastic and well worth the 120 Minute queue!! All other rides were brilliant, the 4d ones out of this world!! Can't wait to go back! No need for young kids, as we traveled as a couple and thoroughly enjoyed every minute!!

We were very lucky with timing but the quality of rides was fantastic and the Harry potter attractions were fabulous. Summer would not be good as Florida is hot and humid. But crowds are down in September and you can get through a lot of the park in one day with an early day pass.

We arrived on a beautiful September morning and were very impressed, much more so than Magic Kingdom. Park seems to be a lot better spaced with an excellent choice of eateries and places to get cold drinks and ice creams. Then came the rain! We were in Daigon alley and so dashed onto the Harry Potter ride, which swiftly broke down. We waited 30 minutes and then came the announcement that the ride was working again. We moved 10ft and then it broke again....so we gave up. This is an indoor ride so I'm not sure why this happened. So, we dashed to the train that links the park to Islands of Adventure, got to the front of the queue, and then the announcement...it had stopped due to bad weather. So, off we trundled on foot to Islands of Adventure. By the time we arrived the sun had come out so we grabbed a bite to eat and then headed to the Sinbad show. There were lots of people waiting but dead on 3pm when the show was due to start....cancelled due to bad weather. Why wasn't this announcement made in advance to save wasted time? We had a great day but it was dampened in the middle by these set backs. There is small print on entrance saying they can't be accountable for the weather which is understandable but when inside rides are breaking down at the same time as rides stopping due to bad weather it is rather frustrating.

My son (13 years) and i went to universal on sun & mon (10/12 & 10/13) and waited in line for over 1.5 hours for the harry potter train ride to be told it wasn't working & they did not know when or if it would be working. And then we went to Diagon Alley to ride the new Harry Potter ride and was told the same exact thing. The next day which was our last day we actually made it on to the new ride for it to break down in the middle of the ride.Never coming back it was totally disappointing.

I went specifically for Harry Potter and those sections of the parks blew my mind. I can only hope my kids can talk my husband into taking us back there eventually! However, my husband is not into Harry Potter and I was counting on the rest of the park to impress him and it's failed miserably. We had a 3 day pass and only went 1 1/2 days. Thumbs up for HP fans and families with kids old enough to enjoy it though!

I love Universal, I must say it does top Disney in my book. Que"s are not bad, it ain't as crowded as disney and it's not as expensive to eat etc. Surprisingly I even found the staff more child friendly. Traveling with a child with ASD, who isn't very good with waiting, crowds etc, they gave me a card which I showed the staff on each attraction which allowed us to take him straight through to the ride. How very thoughtful, it really made his holiday and the rest of the family's too. And the horror night is fantastic too

Went on a Sunday night with wife and another couple, visited 4 houses and spent over four hours in lines waiting. Will not go again, but will return to the Park. If any one does want to go, buy the Fast Pass.

Be sure to ask for a control room tour when you exit Twister. They'll take you into the control room, explain how the show works and let you watch as the ride runs through its program and resets all the effects. The staff were very friendly and extremely helpful. I highly recommend it.

Thought I would try HHN this year and wasnt to bad starting out. Went into the line for the 3rd house and asked what the wait time was and they said it was 45 minutes just like the sign said. We have now been in line over an hour and a half and still not near the front of the line. They keep letting all the Express Pass people in and very little people in the stand by line in. Last time I come to this event!!! Unless you buy the Express pass would not recommend coming to this event!!! I will not be back!
If you can get a day pass and visit both parks, you will not be disappointed. There are so many simulated rides, even those afraid of heights would enjoy this. I know I did.

Lots of fun. Get express passes and save time and limit stress. Diagon Alley and Hogsmeade are great. My 13 yr old didn't want to leave. The detail is incredible. Felt transported. The other areas are OK. Enjoyed the minions. Take your AAA card as most of the sit-down restaurants offer a discount if you have the card. Recommend a 2 -day stay to take it all in.

I highly recommend searching for deals for your tickets. We were able to purchase three days for the price of two, and it was really the perfect amount of time to spend in the two parks. We spend one day at Island of Adventure and two at Universal. The kids bought wands at Universal and we spent about five hours just in the Harry Potter area so they could perform their magic.  While I liked the 4D rides, there are so many of them they got a little predictable after about the third one. The shows were entertaining, but not thrilling. I do wish there were more roller coasters.  What I really appreciated was that my four-year old (who is 41" tall) could ride a majority of the rides and those that he couldn't allowed a parent swap so that we could all wait in line as a family and both my husband and I could ride... and my teen loved it because that meant she got to ride twice.  We went in the middle of November and the lines were so short many were walk-on. The longest wait was 30-minutes for the Gringotts ride. We were glad we didn't spend the extra for the fast pass.  We did stay late one night to watch the parade and light show. It was worth the wait. Very creative and engaging. The kids also enjoyed it.

Its like a cattle market to get in with no organisation at all.  Queues are 2 to 3 hours long within minutes so you are lucky to see three of the 8 haunted houses all night and you will spend 5 plus hours in queues.  Typical hype where they make big promises but just want your money and don't care how many people attend, the more the better in their $$$$$ eyes and they have the audacity to charge you to park as well!!!  DON'T waste your money

Called 2 days prior to arrival to inquire/purchase tickets. 20 minutes on the phone, was convinced to purchase 1day, 2 park ticket with Express Pass for $639.00. We originally thought a 2 day ticket would be the way to go, but the Universal representative's explanation of the Express Ticket convinced us to purchase that ticket.  I was told that I would receive an e-mail confirmation, but that never arrived. Unable to use the self serve kiosk without a confirmation number, we headed to the manned windows to pick up our tickets. The person behind the counter was very friendly, even helping us pick out 4 lanyards for $20.  Our next stop was the entrance turnstiles. Imagine our surprise when our tickets wouldn't work... Off to Guest Services to figure out what went wrong. Discovered that we were sold 4 Express Pass tickets, but that did NOT include admission to the park! It would cost an additional $600+ to purchase 4 admission tickets. Doing some quick math, I realized that it would take a mortgage payment to gain admission to Universal Studios with the Express Pass!!!  Our decision to purchase the Express Pass influenced our decision to change our hotel reservations, so now we can't do the 2 day option even if we wanted.  Adding salt to the wound, we were told that lanyards that we no longer need since we don't have the $650 Express Pass option are non-returnable. Really???  Overall, incredibly disappointed by what I feel is the classic "bait and switch" tactic to get more money from us. My wife and I have saved all year to take our family on this vacation. We couldn't absorb an additional $600+. Now, not only we will be waiting in long lines, but probably won't get on every ride because of the crowds.  Next time in Florida, we will skip Universal Studios and spend the time in Disney, where we have had nothing but positive experiences.  With all of that said, I will be thankful that we are able to spend Christmas in beautiful, sunny Florida!

I love everything from E.T. - The Extra-Terrestrial to the big roller coasters! There is something to please everyone. Warning, the Rocket jerks, especially the second car; I ride with my hands cradling my head to cushion it from the bouncing.
Better buy a "fastpass" if you want to save money or get there early. Not managed as well as Disney but better than legoland.
Went as a family and every one of us loved it. Would recommend going at Halloween for terror nights - words cannot describe!! Fantastic for all ages but especially if you're a thrill seeker like me!

My family and I absolutely loved universal studios.We loved it so much we returned in Nov/14.Bring plenty of spending money as food,drinks, etc can get pricey like any theme park.I would recommend universal studios to my family and friends.

We enjoyed the park very much. It impressed us every day how kind, patient and friendly the staff were- every one of them that we encountered or saw other people speaking with!! It surprised us that some of the 4 D rides were 'vigorous' to ride to say the least! Especially the "minions" ride! Fun, fun, fun!!

It's a nice place in the off season....Just don't go during Halloween nights or around Christmas weeks until after New Years, it's good for a few weeks until mardi crowded nights on the weekends. We have a season pass. Been too all the Disney stuff but we like Universal the best overall the parks here in Orlando. Disney parks are okay if ya never been there, animal kingdom is just like abig zoo but not worth the money to me but a good time is had with kids. For teens go to Unaversal both parks with at least two day pass but three days is better to make it through long lines in the busy season. For example you can wait for Harry Potter rides for 3 hours during busy times or during off season can wait for 30 min. My favorite rides at Universal is all of them! Universal city walk has great places too eat too but bring a big wallet. Everything is overpriced in the whole place, just bring in your back pack a lot of snacks and just split meal. It's all fun.

This attraction is great for young children who do not care if every ride is the same with just a change of characters. There is nothing clever, no surprises, no great fun! One exception: Blues Brothers mini show on the street. Staff were friendly for the most part. The biggest complaint I have is that there is none of learning about how pictures are made, no learning experiences at all. Where is the "adventure" and where is the "excitement?" Not a single "extraordinary" moment. Even the fireworks at the end were what you can see in small town America on any July 4th.

If you go here make sure you get the 2 park hopper ticket to go on the hogwarts express. Especiallu if your a harry potter fan. Such an amazing day. Parade not as good as disney but definately 10 out of 10 for the performers effort.

Valet parking is excellent but universal is noisy, dirty and full of long queues and fed up looking staff. Really disappointed by the whole experience couldn't find anywhere to sit and eat so left about 3pm. Spent my whole life believing the hype and saved long to bring my children. I will try Islands of Adventure as I have stupidly bought 14 day passes for the whole family but have no idea how anyone could spend more than a few hours in this place without going nuts, never will return.

We had been at many of the attractions around Orlando all week and were looking forward to visiting Universal Studios.  We queued up for a while (not too long) and noted the cost for 1 park for a day and though that's a bit expensive considering the size of a park against Disney.  Secondly we noticed that you don't get any free fast passes for rides so have to pay nearly double for this making is ridiculously expensive.  I decided not to go in due to the crowds and price, I'm glad I didn't as fellow travellers said that unless you got a fast pass you waited forever to get on rides.

Went as a family of three adults and two children (ages 8 and 11) over spring break 2015, Booked a vacation package with US airfare, hotel (Universal's Cabana Bay) and three day park passes. No express pass included. Cost:: $7000 total. Express pass was going for $184 per person per day at our hotel. That would have been extra. Went because of Harry Potter attractions. Experienced that, enjoyed the frozen butter beer, and the interactive wands, but won't return This is an uncomfortable park to say the least. We have been to the Disney attractions, Nickelodeon, SIx Flags, Sea World, and Atlantis over prior years spring break. I would return to any one of them but not this one. First, it is Florida and the sun during the day is very hot ( oppressive humidity in the summer months also), You will walk miles and miles in the heat at this park ( one reviewer's pedometer clocked it at 11 miles per day). You will find very few places to sit and rest ( most people were sitting on the curbs in the sun). There were lines for everything including cold drinks. Harry Potter attraction was so mobbed you could hardly walk without banging into someone. The stores there are small so you are standing in lines to get in. Where is the shade and the air conditioning, Universal??? 70 to 120 minute waits for rides (on your feet the whole time) is daunting and longer when a ride malfunctions and several seem to do so every day. Granted, spring break is busy but there needs to be a better way for crowd control, moving people from one end of the park to another, and respite from the sun. Arcade games like you see at state fairs cost $5 per person for a 30 second event. Kids enjoyed the pools at the hotel more than the park. Not all that much to do if you don't like extreme roller coasters or getting soaked to the skin on the water rides. This is a park best enjoyed by teenagers and young adults. For the price, Atlantis was a better value and far more enjoyable.

Dear all, Save up some extra money and visit Orlando Universal Studio. It is 100% worth it! Our family had so much fun. The rides are thrilling and the water rides really get you wet, but no worries you quickly will dry. There is so much to do and to see, so go early and get the VIP pass for front of line, coz the ques are long and waiting time is up to 90 minutes, but with the special pass no more than 5-10 minute so. Please go and have a blast, I promise you will never forget it! We loved it❤️❤️❤️

Visited Universal Florida with my husband and 3 kids (6, 10, 13) during spring break/April 2015. Park was very crowded and lines were long. We did not purchase express passes as they were very expensive ($89-99 per person per day). In fact, the passes were more expensive than the park tickets themselves (we bought 3 day base tickets from AAA for $150 in advance)! We enjoyed all the rides here -- Return of the Mummy was my favorite. Unfortunately, we didn't ride the Despicable Me ride as the line was 110 mins (I'm patient, but not that patient). Didn't stay for the fireworks at park closing -- we could view them from our hotel (Point Orlando --highly recommended). Probably would be best to visit park early or go during non-peak months to avoid long lines. Also, consider staying at a Universal deluxe on-site resort (Royal Pacific or Portofino Bay) b/c express passes are included --> we wanted a larger suite so we decided to stay off-site.

The Harry Potter attractions are fabulous, but there is so much more to do in these side by side parks. You do want to get tickets to both because the Hogwarts train goes back and forth between Islands of Adventure and Universal Studios. It is vital to purchase the "fast" passes if you want to see everything. Well, as it was, I went for 4 days and didn't see everything, but you skip the long lines with a fast pass. The Mummy ride was exceptionally fast and if you get vertigo- skip that one. The Homer Simpson ride was jerky and I just don't get that humor. If you are a Homer fan and ride the big coasters- go for it. Even The Cat in the Hat area was fun for adults. You don't get too wet on the Jurrassic park ride- but you do on the other water rides. Stay at one of the hotels there- you get early admission to the parks. You really DO deserve to have this much fun, no matter how old you are.
My trip over here is remarkable. No words to describe how best the place is ! Every family couple should visit this place for sure.

This is not a review of the theme park - only arrivals at the bus/taxi area and of Universal City walk.  First - we arrived via a car service from our resort on a Friday evening around 6:30. Traffic was very heavy and there were a lot of people milling about in the bus/taxi area. There must have been a hundred buses and the cabs trying to drop off were wrapped around the entire area. The parking attendants were RUDE every single one of them (at least 10 that we encountered) and obnoxious when our car service wanted to drop us off in the designated drop off area. They waived him off, and told him that he couldn't use the drop off area even though the sign clearly said he could. Several were discourteous and you could see their sarcastic laughing as they mockingly told him to "have a nice day - now MOVE". Had I had the opportunity to ask for a badge number, I would have made a personal complaint. It left a bad taste in our mouth that a theme park could make such a bad first impression.  Once we were actually allowed out of the car after looping around a second time, (we had to exit the car quickly as parking attendants were running over to waive the car service around a third time) we ventured upstairs to the City walk. Good variety of music and dining venues - seemed like something for everyone. I hate crowds though and as we were walking towards the restaurants it was like a sea of humanity coming towards us. Very unsettling feeling. I guess if you don't like crowds then Universal is not for you.

We really enjoyed Harry Potter themed Diagon Alley and Hogsmead. The interactive wands were a big hit with our 11, 13, & 14 yr olds. A bit crowded. Ridiculous prices (of course) and a slight resentment toward the Express pass system which made the wait in lines even longer. One plus, we learned on our final day, most all those Snack and Beverage stands will provide cups of complimentary ice water if you ask and it was good. Beats the price of constantly buying bottled water.

Absolutely loved it~ The layout of the place is very similar to other Universal Studios (but that is to be expected) but most of the staff I encountered were friendly and polite. Food booths and location of help stations were convenient and useful; everything was extremely organized! I went there for an event where some of the Harry Potter cast came to the Wizarding World of Harry Potter section of the Park and the organization of the lines and management of customers and staff was well done! No unnecessary lines or space wasted.
Fantastic park, with lots of wonderful things to do and see! The rides are great and the Park was very well kept  We cannot wait to return!

This was our 2nd time visiting as a family. We returned for Diagon Alley and it was worth our long trip. the attention to detail is amazing. The days we were there were rated 9/10 for business, but our longest wait was Despicable Me. I will say, both times we've been, that's been the longest, most brutal wait so if you go and want to ride Despicable Me, just know going into it that it's long and usually hot. I think Universal needs more shade, fans, and misters to help people waiting for this ride. All of those things are provided at Gringott's, where our wait was not that long. Last time we did not have park-to-park passes, but got them this time to ride the Hogwarts Express. Be sure to pay attention when going inside to get on the train as there is a place where they have used mirrors to make it look like people are disappearing into platform 9 3/4! Worth it because 1)the train ride is cool and saves walking when it's 100 degrees and everyone is tired and 2) being able to go over to Islands of Adventure, ride a water ride to get cooled off and then return, was totally worth it. U. Studios doesn't seem to have as many places to get cooled off, but maybe we just missed it this time around. Terminator ride was great and the Mummy is one of our favorites. We took in our own bottled water and snacks, but found out that small cups of ice water are available for free from vendors in the park and they were very nice about giving those out when we asked. Lots of walking, lots of fun!

Just a magical place for any age. You can not do this in 1day. We went for 3days and would have happily done 4 if we had the time and energy. All the staff are lovely. The themes just fantastic. The thrill rides are great and worth the wait. The water rides are just as thrilling as the coasters.  It's worth the money.  The only negative is the line cutters. Not the parks fault as it happens everywhere.

Harry Potter brought to life! It's amazing and I'm so glad we went! We visited Islands of Adventure/Hogwarts the year it opened up and were so excited to read that Universal Studios opened up Diagon Alley! It looks just like the movie and how you would imagine it from reading the books. All the shops are creative and imaginative and just amazing to see. My kids were so excited to visit Ollivanders because they watched so many You Tube videos of kids getting picked to test the wands. I warned them they might not be picked! It's not random! Whoever the first kid is in the room, the Wizard will line about 5 of you up on a row, positioning kid #1 in the front of the room. That kid is the one who gets picked to flick the wand and say the spells. It's very cool. We went through twice and timed it so we were first in line. Luckily it was a rainy day and not too crowded. Gringotts was cool mostly because it brings you into the movie. They've made the wait in line an experience by itself with all the goblins around and special props. That aside, the Transformers and Spiderman sims were our favorite! So much fun. The Minion sim is funny. My best advice is don't forget stuff like sunblock, an umbrella...because if you buy the stuff in the park - which is fun to do but SO expensive - you will pay triple the normal cost. If you're not staying at a theme park hotel, invest in the fast pass! It was so much fun to jump to the front of the line. It sucks to wait in line for so long. And this is Orlando, so expect thunderstorms in the afternoon.

Wow wow wow, this place is one of the best I have ever been to. Not a dull moment to be had fills me with excitement and sure does get the adrenalin going. This year I am going for the forth time. Cannot wait. Fun for all ages with plenty of excitement to be had.

I have to say I really enjoyed this park. The section of the park that has Harry Potter is awesome. The store fronts and alley look just like it did in the movie. The have an awesome feature for kids and adults too had fun with this. You purchase a wand from the store and there are spots within Dragon Alley that are marked where you stand with the wand and move the wand in the direction that this icon on the pavement shows you and you make things turn on. Water fountains turn on, rain fall, puppets play, etc. Real fun. The actual ride was awesome. The effects were awesome and the bank you walk through looks like it did in the movie. The transformers ride was another of my favorites. The Simpsons section of the park was cool too. They have a Moes Tavern where you can go grab a drink at the bar and go grab a bite to eat. The lines in the park are typical. Sometimes a 40 minute wait other times up to 65 mins. But the lines keep moving and they have it set up so that there is always something to look at while waiting in line. Seems like it goes by fast. All in all we enjoyed all the rides. The cost per ticket is a little high. Wish it was a little cheaper and we would go back and visit again soon.

This place is incredibly overrated. The rides are minimally interesting at best, save for the fact that the themes are based on Universal movies that are well liked and remembered. There are no truly scary rides, therefore it is a park that is best suited for young children and people who scare easily.

Great rides but long waits. You can pay double to get the fast pass. I constantly felt like they were taking every dollar they could. They charged much more than the products were worth but there were memorable events.
My husband and I are movie buffs so we opted for a honeymoon at Universal. Totally worth it! The park had everything we could ask for. We're already planning our next trip :D

We were pretty disappointed this year on vacation. Took 2 teens and the lines were crazy. You know to expect everything to cost a lot... but we didn't feel we got our money's worth. We went in late August. Didn't buy the Express passes. If you stay at one of their hotels it's included. Maybe that would have been better. Blue Man Group was awesome though.

I must admit it's been a few years since I have been to a theme park & forgotten how bad the lines R, but if the ride is worth it can make up for it. This brings me to one of the worst rides in Orlando, how Universal can put this out just shows they really don't care how they get your $$ out of your pocket.  Well on to the experience itself, after our family of 5 had stood in line for around 40 minutes ( not bad over the entire parks lines ) we boarded the great looking train for what we thought would be a great treat, I mean who wouldn't want to ride the famous Hogwarts Train. I believe we paid a extra $35 bucks per adult, I can't recall if there is a discount for kids.  WHAT A WASTE OF MY HARD EARNED $$, the short ride to basically nowhere consist of basically a real nice TV up against the carriage window showing a short movie featuring the characters from the movies as the train moves the 1000 yds between parks.  Lets not forget that to even do this you have to buy a two park pass for the one day. You can walk out the main entrance of either park & enter the other in less than ten minutes & save hundreds of $$.  DON"T DO IT, no matter how much the kids beg, you will kick yourself.  Another thing, the locker situation is a absolute nightmare, you might want to think about renting one a day & use it as a base instead of putting your items up at every ride that requires it.  The TSA have a number of people working the coaster lines, when they say nothing in your pocket, they mean it. You get passed the first guy, but they have metal detectors & staff with wands just like the airport, some of these guys really love their job.  This comment is for anyone working at Universal who would hope keep up with Tripadvisor. The lines were driving me crazy, so I was going to get us all Fast Pass tickets. These are close to or right at a $100 bucks WOW. But get this, we had the two park pass, paid for the stupid train & they wanted another $400's + to get around faster right.  The Fast Pass was ONLY VALID AT ONE PARK, WHAT THE HELL.  A fast pass is a fast pass, why is it not valid in both parks, it's not as if we could be in two lines at once in both parks, this blew my mind.  NEVER EVER AGAIN.
We went on a Saturday and it was extremely crowded with the longest lines I have ever encountered. One ride broke down and we have to get off and walk after waiting in said long line!!!!

We have gone to Rock the Universe for years and not been disappointed. Be prepared to spend $17 per vehicle for parking. We have always been in a nice parking garage which is easy to navigate. The walk from parking to Universal is about average for a theme park. Once inside the park is well laid out. We love the Christian artists who are performing through the park and the rides/restaurants are open. Friday nights are not usually as busy as Saturday nights. The only negative I can think of is it rains almost every year. The event has never been rained out since we have been going but it does cause a few delays.

I broke my own electric wheelchair while in the park. It took hours for them to understand that I wasn't going to just get up an walk away. They would not help fix the chair or provide me with transportation back to my on site Hotel. We never got to use our second day tickets.

Universal Studios is a sure bet for fun and entertainment for all ages. There are rides from easy to thrilling and stage and street shows. They even have a make up / horror show that's wonderful. The new Harry Potter additions are a sure hit as well and Gringotts is well worth the wait in line. Enjoy your day! !

We came in on october 5. In the web page they posted closing time 9.00 pm a month in advance, the day we came in the map said 8.00 pm and then the crew said it was actually 7.00 pm. Its horrible that they let you plan and spend in advance but change schedules while you are in the park. That is just a scam. This does noy happen at disney, really. And even more with the ridiculously expensive tickets.

great day out with the family... I do think it's a bit unfair to charge for parking on top of a very expensive ticket into the park, however once in you forget and just enjoy the day... Harry Potter is amazing and well worth the visit alone. I do wish they had more variety of food to have instead of just burgers, especially for the kids

Universal Studios Orlando was so much fun! Easy to get in and the Expess Pass was great as we never waited any longer than 30 minutes for any ride and those rides were The Simpsons and Shrek. The Simpsons was the most surprising ride to us; my sister got a tad woozy, the only experience that created such uneasiness. Plenty of food options digging the turkey legs, churros etc. We loved the following five experiences: The Minions, The Mummy, Rip Ride Rocket, Transformers and Harry Potter. So much fun and well designed as it was easy walking and orderly picking your route. The Makeup Show was fun and gave you a break.  Such a great day. Enjoy Universal Studios Orlando!

We went to Universal for the day while passing thru Orlando, we had a great time. We arrived at 8am when they opened and the lines were very short, we were able to get in a few rides before the lines got too long. Transformers was by far my favorite ride all day.

Not a HP fan but the area is fantastic. Great themeing and visuals. The dragon is amazing and the shops equally so. Gringotts ride very good, a new concept in theme park rides. The rest of the park just doesn't do it for me. Transformers rides is essentially the same as Spider Man in IoA and Minions/Simpsons is also essentially the same - a simulator ride. Rip Ride Rock It is a great concept but the ride really shook me up and hurt my neck and head and I am a thrill junkie. Did not go on it again.
I have been before but the Harry Potter section was new, could have spent all day in there. Fire breathing dragon too!

We came to Universal on a blistering hot day during the first week in November - the hottest temperatures for that week ever. Disney filled most of our days, but we did give one day over to Universal to see Harry Potter. Universal is dependent on the rides, and because of my back problems we couldn't get on any of them. It seems designed for 14 year old boys, so if you're one of those, enjoy.  Universal is not Disney. It's not even close in terms of comfort, class and value. The exhibits (less Harry Potter) are tired and in desperate need of an upgrade.  We were in need of directions several times. Disney has employees scattered all over, ready and willing to offer help. There was NO ONE in sight at Universal, every time we needed help. We finally entered restaurants and asked the hosts. Mostly, they didn't know the answer to our questions.  Harry Potter was ingenious and fun, although crowded, shoulder to shoulder with school kids and parents (first week in November - does anybody still go to school?) We took the Hogwarts Express to the companion park, Island of Adventure, which was a complete disappointment. It was so hot we were desperate to return to the main park, but... the train broke down.  I asked the attendant how we were supposed to return. She hadn't a clue, other than to tell us to walk to the other side of this park, cross over, and walk around to the main park. This trip was perhaps a half mile to a mile in 95 degree heat. My wife was fading. Could you offer a golf cart or anything to replace the train? Disney would have done that. You can rent a wheelchair, we were told. When my wife looked like she was going to pass out, they comped the wheelchair out of pity or fear of a lawsuit. I was then faced with the walk back to the main park. I've had a stroke, spinal stenosis and two shoulder rebuilds, so I was the last person to be pushing this wheelchair, but it was ALL that was available. It simply had to be done.  I arrived back at the main park an hour later and collapsed onto a bench. There were no attendants in sight to offer any help. After while I got up and we entered an air conditioned show which revived us. We saw a completely lame parade, nothing compared to Disney, and ate dinner at the single worst restaurant I've ever encountered: Monster Burger. The burgers were hockey pucks, overpriced, self-served on cafeteria trays and eaten in a room full of soda vending machines on a concrete floor which offered echoes of the mostly young diners' shouting.  Never again in this life. And we paid a fortune for the day!
Even if the line is 5 minutes I'd skip this. It's an old dated ride that's environmentally preachy and it just doesn't do anything. The good thing is the kids won't be scared on the ride.

It's been 20 years since my last visit to Universal, it's changed and not for the good. Gone is the true Universal purpose - movies and all things associated. It's been replaced by booming music and big rides. The bigger the ride the better. It's lost all of it's charm.  The cost to enter for two adults for one day and access to both parks was $500.00 USD. The value is simply not there. Parking was an additional $20.00.  The roller coasters were fun but all of the movie related rides are gone as is the backlot tour which was the charm of Universal.  The best part if by far Harry Potter even for someone who has never read one of the books or seen a movie. But it will cost you admittance to both parks. Anything Harry Potter related is not included in the Express Pass.  We've done it but won't do it again. We still choke over the cost of admittance for the day.

We were there with our 2 teenage daughters during the Christmas week of 2015. It was crowded but that's when my kids have school off. For $10 more a person, I got us 3-day park-to-park tickets which I'm really glad I did. With all the people there and my husband having a bad back, we just took it easy on all 3 days to visit the parks. I did not get the express tickets because only my older one loves the roller coasters (she only rode on a few by herself and she probably only really loved one, we are from Ohio and she's used to the Cedar Point great roller coasters and doesn't care too much for the simulators that many of them are at Universal). But if you are into the rides, it would save you a lot of time getting the express pass, even during the Christmas week when there were so many people. With 3 days, we went to the park around 9-10am and stayed until 4-5pm. Long enough day for us. I think they do a great job with all the shows and the buildings and structures. Loved our visit.

Having been going to Disney for years and this year we decided to go to Universal Studios particularly for the Harry Potter exhibits. We loved Diagon Alley and the Escape from Gringots ride. The architecture was good at Hogsmead but otherwise found this attraction area a disappointment. While interesting in concept Hogwarts Express was not worth the line wait. We had the unlimited tickets so went through the rest of the parks in pretty quick order. In hind sight we should have gotten the unlimited park to park tickets and covered both parks easily in one full day. We will not go back again since we feel there aren't enough quality rides but we're glad we checked the box of the Potter rides.

Family of 9 travelling from the UK - 8 Adults 1 child. I have visited this park several times over the past 25 years during the christmas holiday period and I have never seen a park so busy with ridiculous wait times for all attractions. Harry Potter world looked great from what we managed to see of it amongst all the crowds. Literally could not walk yet alone attempt to push a stroller. Staff not able to control lines, we left after just one hour. Do not waste money unless going off peak!

My wife and I, both in our late 60s, had a brilliant time. Not being interested in fast roller coasters we chose this, more sedate, attraction. It was well worth the money, despite being sneezed on by Donkey in the Shrek 4D attraction, and the rain which was incessant during the afternoon.
Diagon Alley was such a special place. It was exactly like the movie and so fun to walk through. I highly recommend visiting if you are an HP fan.

Still the best park for rides. Gringotts ride was brilliant. We had Butterbeer with a whisky shot. Well worth it. Harry Potter is very crowded. Transformers ride is really good and The Mummy is always. Favourite. If it's busy get in the solo rider line, so much quicker. And you sometimes still get to sit in the same car. We found character photo opportunities easy. A lot smaller lines than Disney. We got some great photos with Transformer Megatron.

The facility was very clean and well designed. It was quite small for The Orlando area but was equal in cost to the other attractions that are available in the same area. That made it a poor choice if the other attractions were part of a family choice. The walk from the parking lot to the attraction was very long and the parking was a little chaotic.
The ticket price was confusing on-line and the staff at the ticket counters took forever and seemed to be car salesmen. Long waits and unfriendly staff. Would not return or recommend to anyone.

Having paid $30 for premier parking... We walked for an hr to the Universal Park we'd come to visit. Premier parking was in the furthest lot from the entrance to Universal.... Then you have to wander thru all the theme venus, restaurant areas, gift shops, stop to get assistance, and fumble with a less than user friendly map. Getting out of the park was no easier...

I was so excited for Universal. I have 3 boys... 11, 9 & 6... The two oldest were definitely growing out of Disney. For what I paid.... For 2 days (got 3rd day free)... NO PARK HOPPER (that would be additional $50/ticket.... And no fast pass)... It was $900.... Add parking & food... Omg!!! AND HONESTLY... besides the Minion Ride.... That had ATLEAST a 60 min wait... The mummy roller coaster, and the Rock It roller coaster.... It was OUTDATED!!!!!!! The 3D (& 4D) technology for Shrek, Simpsons, Terminator, and Transformers is old!!!! It will be awhile before (& IF) I return. Not impressed at all.

Several rides closed or 'under construction' Restaurants all rammed full with long waits to just get in Park closes at 1900hrs for corporate activities I was disappointed in the lack of any real inteest for film buffs - just cheesy rides and plastic backdrops. maybe I expected too much, but for the entry price I expected much, much more - not a ratio of approx 20 tat outlets for ever ride

I was shocked at how poor our experience was at this park. Most surprising is that Universal is 80% trinket shops and subpar eating establishments and only 20% rides and amusements. Signage is shockingly poor and there is almost no staff to help getting around. The park, in essence, is very poorly managed. Park tickets are expensive enough but Universal deems it necessary to charge a minimum of $20 for parking...I found this the final outrage. The only slightly positive was Diagone Alley which was an exact replica from the movie BUT it is really designed to sell overpriced trinkets (expect to spend a MINIMUM of $40 for a wand made in China). I would never return...I felt ripped-off from the moment I entered Unuversal to the moment I left. You've been warned!

The park was a messy. Garbage for all place. Staff rude and the restroom at Jurrasic park was so dirty that was impossible to be used. The park was crowded and the wait time does not correrponded to the real time that you must to wait. In an attraction that was marked 60 minutes the wait time lasted even for 2 hours. People in the Express way went on and out repeatedly in the same attraction as the other people who were on the waiting list and does not paid for the express way but also paid for the ticket were let aside. In eight hours at the park I was able to visit just 4 attractions . It was a waste of time and money and I felt stupid. Universal Orlando Resort?? Never more. Já fui algumas vezes a este parque, mas desta vez ele estava imundo, mal sinalizado e os atendentes se portavam de forma absolutamente rude. Os banheiros do food court do Jussaric Parque estavam tao sujos que era impossivel usa-los. Não bastasse isto no sistema de express way adotado por eles as pessoas entram e saem de um brinquedo repetidas vezes passando na frente daquele que se encontram na fila de espera e se nao pagaram por este passe pagaram seu ingresso no parque que nao é barato: 100 dolares. É um desperdicio de tempo e dinheiro. A proposito, o expresso do Harry Porter é ABSOLUTAMENTE ridiculo, não vale a espera de mais de uma hora. Voce entra numa cabine e simplesmente passa um filminho na janela do trem, absolutamente sem emoção.

Such a shame we were looking forward to visiting this park but found the staff ignorant! Rude! And totally unfriendly! Ride times were over 100 mins! As we stayed in a resort hotel we entered park at 7am to get to Harry Potter section of park but even so the place soon filled up! Beware Wizarding World of Harry Potter was so over priced! Had a drink of Duff and the server refused to serve us again because we didn't leave a tip after the first one!! Ha ha saved us a fortune that day!! Park was littered and had filthy toilets which had run out of toilet paper by early afternoon. Seemed the characters were outdated as my daughter only recognised the Simpsons and minions! The only saving grace was the Leaky Couldron which served a lovely English Breakfast! If only they didn't serve a cousant with it?

We went here and Islands of adventure on a 3d park pass. This only got 1 of our days and was enough. A bit more dated than Islands and no water rides. Hulk roller coaster was down (will be for months) so we unfortunately didn't get a chance to try that one. Our favorite ride was Transformers!

If you have older kids or if you are an older "kid", this is the place for you. I thoroughly enjoyed myself. My recommendations are Shriek, Terminator, The Horror Make-up Show (it's hilarious) and the Simpson's. You can spend the whole day and not see and fully enjoy everything, so get a two-day pass!!!

We went to Universal on a Sunday. Looked forward to just the two of us being there. It ended up costing $512 for the day. Two park passes and express. We went to the Harry Potter world and they weren't even honoring the express pass. They said everyone has the same wait. Wow. We paid $89 each for this convenience. Too busy. Not worth the money and especially not the extra express pass. :(

I have been to Universal several years ago, and it was just OK. But in May when I visited I noticed a HUGE positive "grown up" Universal Studios. I was pleasantly surprised! There is so much to do there now and their Express Pass makes waiting in lines for 1 1/2 hours a thing of the past. Our express pass was part of our on-site hotel package, but I would have paid for it for sure. We walked by so many people waiting in long lines, and our adventures were so much more pleasant because of this. The park is clean and organized and easy to find things in. We had a blast there!

Fantastic park with plenty of great rides. Transformers ride was excellent as well as rip ride rocket. Bought the photo pass and got some great pics really worth it. Would recommend getting the giant Simpsons donut

Watch out when you purchase tickets on the site-they advertise that you get a coupon book but when you pick them up at the front office they tell you they never had a coupon book. When I picked up mine at the end of feb 2016 I didnt get one let alone the envelope supposedly that was waiting for me. All I got were the tickets. I only printed out 1 copy also -print out a second one to have on hand to verify that's what was said. I just went on their site to look at their deals for hotels since I am going their in oct 2016 and already have my annual tickets. It is again on their site about a free coupon book when you order the tickets online. spoke on the chat and told this and they wanted a copy of the reciept and what site I found this on. She didnt know it's on their own site. this is not right at all.

Stood in line on a ride for an hour, and watched them stop all but the express pass riders.  A disappointed 9 year old couldn't understand, and its is hard to explain the greed behind this.  On vacation again this year and US is not on the list.
This is a great place for young and old. Great rides, great shows and great live performances. The free drink refills are a great idea.

My wife and I never get date time with two small children. When she surprised me this morning with a brief day date to Universal I was thrilled. She paid for a babysitter, just for a few hours, so we could ride the new attraction " skull island, reign of Kong". After parking and rushing through the crowds to get to the ride, we see a 90min wait. Knowing that we had limited time, we agreed that this was the one ride for us to wait for. 45 minutes in, we hear there will be a brief delay, we wait. It comes back up, then 30 min later, another brief delay, and we wait. Then we are told there is an extended delay, and then an announcement that the ride is down, and will be at least 40min until operational. We had already been there the 90min and were not able to wait any longer, and regretfully had to leave. I stopped at guest services to explain our situation, and hoped for at least a fast pass for a later date. Instead we are told that since we chose to leave the line, "there is nothing they can do". I find that hard to believe. Being in the service industry myself, I know better. However, because I know better, I left without causing a scene. Needless to say, I am very dissatisfied with the supposed "guest service" and will not be renewing our annual passes if this is how business is done. I'm not looking for hand outs, just a chance to redo a brief day date with my wife.
Always a good walk-bring good shoes! Always expensive-water and drinks especially over priced! However we find it better than Disney-and a little cheaper!

We chose Universal as our kids had been to several of the other parks on previous trips to Orlando. Our boys are 8 & 9, so too old for the kiddie rides but not quite tall enough for the roller coasters at other parks. We thought Universal would be good because they were tall enough for everything they offer.  Showed up and two adult/two kids passes with FastPass came to $927. Sticker shock.  We entered and the FastPass lines weren't much better than the regular lines. Worse, the place is about as worn out as it gets....reminded me of a cheesy place somewhere in Myrtle Beach.  The roller coaster is good but beyond that, very unimpressive. The Mummy ride was okay, at best and otherwise it's just a bunch of those rides where they put a movie screen in front of you, 3-D goggles on your face, and the chair moves around in an effort to trick your brain into thinking you're on a ride.  I will say that the Harry Potter section is interesting but if you're not into HP, it's whatever. Even if you are into it, not enough to justify an afternoon there.  Finally, no energy whatsoever compared to any of the Disney parks. No music, no characters, nothing inspiring. Avoid at all costs.

Have visited here many times before and feel the addition of Diagon Alley and Kings Cross station with the Hogwarts Express between both parks is great. We moved between the 2 parks throughout the day and found it so much better as we could take the train each time and the queues were only about 10 mins each time. We were disappointed that the Hulk Ride was shut as its being upgraded, but really want to return next year as it was the best ride and so hopefully it will be even better.  One main criticism, please can the park provide more seats for people waiting for members of their party who are queuing for rides. I no longer go on roller coasters and have an injury and found that I struggled to find seating whilst waiting for my family. The worst of the lot is the ride Rip Ride Rocket, this is no where to sit, and NO SHADE so I felt quite ill by the time my family came off the ride.

I have been to this park many times but today had issues I want to share so that others may not experience the same problems. Firstly avoid the rip off parking charges do not upgrade your parking. Just pay the normal rate you still get to the parks. Buy your tickets before visiting as I will tell you the issues with this. After clearing security we then formed into the queue to purchase the tickets. Needless to say this was slow as the staff were wanting to sell add on features. After an hour yes an hour got to the staff member ordered the tickets then handed credit card. Sorry cannot accept this without your passport. Who takes a passport to a theme park ? Next when proved a point that it is not a requirement to show a passport to use visa, and having purchased meals in the park with a credit card where no ID was required. Staff member then went into robot mode, have you any photo ID again I said it was not necessary as used card here days earlier and not required. Then the usual happens when faced with not in the script then says to a supervisor I have an issue with this man. I am now an issue not a customer.So by now I am not happy, directed to guest relations, who said it was policy to ask for ID when using credit card. Sorry used card in Universal Boardwalk no one asked for ID. Also pointed out to staff that no where does it state on entrance that I D is required to use a credit card. As we where meeting friends in park could I get a message to them to tell them we would be delayed. Sorry no can do. At this point even if I had ID no way was I giving them my money. Oh it took me another 45 minutes to get to see someone at guest services. For a park that prides itself on new rides maybe they could invest in chip and pin ?  So walking back to the car saw another guest service who were helpful in that they placed a message on. Their customer service screen that if friends asked for us they would find out we were unable to join them. Thanks staff. Universal how come I can buy merchandise and food bill using credit card without ID but not tickets can you explain ?  Or was it today your staff member got out the wrong side of bed and became a jobsworth ?  So to all visitors take ID just in case and enjoy yourselves if you get in. If you speak sense and put forward reasonable arguments do not expect the same in return. You will be met with a robotic reply.  Thank you Universal for ruining a family and friends day out.

Arrived at noon and had to join a queue to purchase entry. After waiting 20 minutes and we didn't move an inch, we joined another queue. Another 20 minutes passed until we finally were at the front of the queue. This is unacceptable.  As we were only there for the day we purchased tickets for both parks and Express. For 3 adults and 1 child the cost was over $1100!!!! Madness.  We paid begrudgingly and went through the pay booths only to have to join another queue to have our bags checked and then scan our entrance tickets. Enough queueing already!!! This took another 10 minutes...  Express wasn't exactly useful. You jumped a few people but then we're merged into the regular queue which caused friction sometimes with others waiting in the queue who would do their best not to let you in.  We only attended the Shrek 4D in this park and decided to move on to the other park. I'm glad we did as the wait for the Hogwarts train took at least 45 minutes queueing. Bonkers.  When we finally got to the other park we discovered it was over crowded and walking around was stressful and not a great experience. We rode on about 6 rides and by this point it was 9 pm and time to go. We went to the Hogwarts Express and discovered the queue was winding outside of the building and stated a 45 minute wait. Having had enough we asked a staff member how we get out. Unfortunately it was a long walk but no where near as long as a 45 minutes wait while staring into space.  This place is a horrendous. Avoid if you can.

Excellent family vacation spot. Great for everyone. First trip was in 2003, was with wife's family. Mother in law is wheel chair bound, and almost every ride she is capable of enjoying. Of course as any there are a few exceptions. I have been 3 times total over the years, each time it gets better. I do miss a few of the old rides, but with limited area to grow, I completely understand the need to update to keep the parks from getting stale. I could move to central Florida if my wife would let us, just to go more often.

We had 4 day tickets to Universal Orlando, spent 2 of the 4 at this park. This has been a long time favorite park of mine, with us returning every time we visit the Orlando area. This visit was far below normal standards. Within our first hour in the park, THREE different rides broke down, all three only after a very long wait in each of the three lines. I know things happen but to have our day start this way really set the unfortunate tone for the whole day. We noticed that the que areas and also sets for some of the rides had damage to them (done intentionally from guests), with all of the money that this park brings in on a daily basis I left there really wondering why they don't seem to bother keeping the park looking nice and better maintaining the rides, both to ensure a better guest experience. Not to compare parks but Disney would NEVER allow an area to look anything less than perfect and maintained. Really disappointed this time.
4th of July: crowd, hot, no fireworks and no easy to get out, about 2.000 people wants to leave the park and the doors closed, was not only annoying was also dangerous
Great place. The kids love it, as do their parents. Gringetts, Minnions, Simpsons, The mummy, great fun. Go early and beat some of the queues. $20 per day parking adds up.

I have used the VIP Services at Universal 3 times in Florida and once in California. It is truly the best way to experience a theme park. The Perks included in your experience: 1. Valet Parking - NO line ups, safe and convenient! 2. Continental Breakfast - Muffins and other sweet pastries, cereal, whole fruit, coffee, tea, hot chocolate. They also have free bottles of water for you to grab for the day. 3. Ponchos - for rain or for the wet rides! 4. Guide - this is the best part! I have never had the same guide and therefore, never had the exact same experience. They all come with their own tidbits of information though. Inside info and places that the rest of park goers cannot see or hear about. 5. Front of the line for all major rides - this is NOT Express Pass. This is back door into the attraction directly to the front of the line. No waiting. 6. Food Voucher Card - We were able to get 1 quick service meal (no sit down to be served restaurants), 2 drinks and one snack/dessert. I didn't end up spending a cent on food or parking the whole day. 7. Unlimited Express Pass - after the tour was over (about 5 or 6 hours) our VIP card allowed us to go through the express pass for all the rides that offer it for the remainder of the day. Not as fast as when you are with the guide, but 10 -15 mins wait, rather than an hour or 2. 8. Discount - after your tour, your VIP card gets you discounts on your purchases in stores.  Tips: a) Book ahead as busy times can fill up. b) If you have a big enough group, get the private tour c) Do both parks. You have the time, might as well save money and just go the one day. You will HATE having to wait in line after you haven't. d) If your guide does a great job, tip them! e) Be ready to walk a lot! You don't want to be the one slowing the rest of the group down. d) Shop and take photos after the tour. This tour is so you can get on as many rides as possible with the shortest wait. Do that stuff after, you will have time. e) Don't be late! This includes in the morning as well as after lunch. You are holding up other families :)  ***Additional ways to save*** -For anyone visiting Universal with an American Express Credit Card- *Use your card to buy your tickets and you will have access in to the American Express Lounge. It is a nice, air conditioned room with tv and couches as well as drinks and snacks. This was all free to us, just for having an Amex. -If you have an AMA or CMA card *Discounts given on food and merchandise purchases.

Visited Universal Studios with family - 6 adults and 4 children in April 2016. Spent one day (thank goodness that was all) there. Food lines were horribly long and took F-O-R-E-V-E-R. the food itself was just OK. I waited in one line where there were 7 people in line ahead of me, it took 45 minutes to get a drink! Seems that the person working the stand was more interested in asking everyone where they were from, if they had any grandchildren and talking about her grandchildren. I heard the same comments and questions 6 times before I got to the front of the line. Similar issue with lunch where the lines were SLOW moving. I do not complain when there is a reason for long/slow lines, but they were not that busy that day and seemed to have more than enough help to process the orders. Once we finally got the food it was just OK. The 'other' Orlando venue was great in both lines and food quality aspects.
Love all the rides at Universal. The food is great, staff is nice. worth the price of tickets. bring your own food.
The place is fantastic, a week wouldnt be enough time to see this place through. For a comic fan like myself it's an absolute dream to go here, the spiderman ride and Hulk are absolutely phenomenonal
Great park for what you are paying. Tons to do, and many great places to eat inside the park, and very reasonably priced.

Universal and island of adventure:  - The parking is great 20$, 30$ preferred. - The staff have this great attitude, really nice. -Thrills, are awesome, HULK the best, Dragon Challenge spectacular, the ReVenge of the MUMMY spectacular, Hollywood Rip Ride Rockit awesome. - 3Ds, Forbidden Journey is awesome, Transformers great, Escape from Gringotts very cool, King Kong really cool. Water attractions, you could buy a poncho and you will be really fine, no need to carry more clothes.  Overall, Universal is superior Walt Disney parks for adults, obviously children would love Disney!!!

So we spent 1 day here last year and weren't impressed. This year we spent 3 days here and had a BLAST!! We did everything (except Hulk which was closed and Rocket) we thoroughly enjoyed The Wizarding World of Harry Potter. Those rides were crazy!!! The funniest part was that we found ourselves ducking into rides we may not have thought about going on just to get out of the heat...then found that the ride was excellent!! Hubby did not feel that Kong was worth the 90 minute wait however. If you must do it and it's still hot in Orlando, do it at night like we did. Otherwise, had an awesome time and we will probably be back in a few years. We just hope they don't kill the E.T. ride by then, we still love it!!!

Stay to the right when entering the city walk entrance to go to the studios, you will see the Famous universal globe and arches.Studios feels more adult based with lots of architecture, shops and streets. There are rides such as transformers, MIB, escape from gringrotts, E.T, Simpsons, shrek, minions, plus diagon alley with the fire dragon and shops. You can get the hogwarts express at kings cross to islands of adventure which is also a good experience.

Went to Halloween Horror Nights. Planned the night out, paid for the fast pass. Everything going as planned and then you get to the end of your visit, 1 ride to go. What? ! The Harry Potter ride is closed 2 hours before the park closes. They said it closes early so they can get it ready to open early in the morning. So I guess the morning ticket holders are more important. If I would have known ahead of time, we would have gone there first. I feel cheated and it kinda left a sour note to the whole experience. Shame on you Universal.

Had to purchase a pass to be enable to ride attractions. The Harry Potter ride needs to be changed to ensure larger guest can ride. How hard could it be to have some seats that could accommodate these guest. I saw one woman rather large be told she could ride and my husband and grandson were told no because of their size. They are larger build but definitely not huge. to me this discrimination against people that are of larger build, unless they are charged a lesser amount, they should be able to ride as anyone else. My husband and grandson were embarrassed.

We drove down from Minnesota for my brother's birthday, and we will never return. Staff was rude and egotistical, the majority of attractions were shut down or broke down during operation, food is overpriced, and wait times are long.
We enjoyed this place more than we even imagined we would. The rides were incredible. You have to ride the Transformers ride

Theme parks are expensive vacations, so plan your trip well! I signed up for deals on the Universal site months ago and did end up getting a "buy one day and get two days free" deal that I was able to use for our family of four park to park.  Spaced out our 3 days between IoA and Universal, making sure to do my research in advance. Did not need to do one full day morning to night at either park, was great to break it up over time.  For those who get motion sick, I highly recommend taking something before going on any rides. I had to load up before each visit into the park or risk making myself very sick. The teenagers were fine, but we did avoid The Simpson ride, since it made my teen queasy last year.  Express pass is a huge help and not sure I could give a 4 star rating if we didn't have it, since the wait times looked long for regular park visitors. Even on a Saturday, did not have to wait long. But be aware that Gringots in Diagon Alley does not have a fast pass, so we did that ride first thing in the morning with an early entry for resort guests. Harry Potter and The Forbidden Journey in IoA also does not take express passes either.  The biggest hassle I had was with the old school paper park tickets and express passes. My spouse refused to wear a lanyard, so I had to keep his park passes in mine, otherwise risk them getting lost. Having to scan your park pass and give the correct thumb or finger print each time you entered got a little old. (Disney bands are nice in this regard.) It also held up the lines frequently with passes getting mixed up or someone not remembering which finger or hand they used for the print. Hopefully Universal will upgrade this system at some point. With the two parks being so close and Hogwarts Express adding another mode to move inbetween parks, it would be nice to have some sort of express lane or faster method for park to park guests. Felt like I was constantly taking out my original park ticket which is separate from the express pass. Had to also keep my room key handy for early entry. My spouse never figured it all out and needed me to state what was needed and when.  As far as rides reviews, we enjoyed everything we singled out as "must do". There were a few misses, such as the Animal Actors, cute and interesting but not sure it was worth the time. The Terminator show was pretty lame and I'd for sure skip that one altogether. The 3D used is so old that it didn't even feel like 3D. Plus the Terminator franchise is kinda dated, my teens had no interest even during the show. The only ride that seemd over hyped was Kong, but was still fun. Not sure I woud've enjoyed it had we waited hours. Worth a 20 min wait maybe, but not much more in my opinion.  Favorite ride for my teens was The Mummy, they went on it muliple times. We also enjoyed all the popular rides like Gringots, Spiderman, transformers, Hulk, Rock it, Jurassic Park river raft (did get wet) and Despicable Me. Favorite show was the Horror Make-up show, which was very funny.  Sad that it might be a long time before we go again, but felt like I got a chance to see and do everything we wanted. If more time, would've stayed for a second Duff beer and maybe eat inside Moe's Tavern.

Other than the Harry Potter section, which was really wonderful, I found Universal Studios to be a BAD version of Disney World. If you go to Universal, I highly suggest you ONLY visit Harry Potter and then save the rest of your time and energy for Disney. You will probably be tempted - like we were - to mill around the rest of Universal after you see Diagon Alley, because after all you paid to get in and it can't really be that bad... right? Wrong.  Why? Really, it comes down to one thing: the quality of execution at Universal Studios is just really, really poor. The rides are convoluted and many of them are very similar. Almost all the rides we experiences involved sitting in a "car" and being shook around by hydraulics in front of a 3D screen. Add in a blast of hot air in your face when something exciting happens and a sprinkle of water and you've basically described all of the new rides in the park. Even worse, things like the volume or "how long should the employee talk to me at the intro" were REALLY POORLY THOUGHT OUT. One ride we went on had a huge group of people standing in a room for like 15 minutes while an employee screeched (they were in "character") and literally tried to annoy people as part of their schtick. The crowd got agitated and rude by the time we were let in the ride. Why would anyone think that was a good idea? Another ride had sound effects so loud that I genuinely think caused damage to people's hearing. I thought it was just me, but other people were complaining as well when exiting the ride. Another annoying, poorly thought out detail: after the parade, workers with lawn-mower type machines literally started weaving through the crowd vacuuming up the debris sent out by the parade floats. I get that they have to clean it up, but couldn't you find a way to do it that doesn't involve running a lawnmower type device right by me and all these kids?  The stores / merch were complete junk. It seems like Universal just outsources everything - the quality of the items and even the packaging varied wildly by the item. Pretty much the only items that were pretty decent across the board was the Harry Potter stuff, and I bet Universal's team didn't have much to do with that.  Long story short, GO FOR HARRY POTTER and LEAVE! The rest is no better than a permanent fair. And a kind of sad fair at that.

Visited the park for one day to check out Harry Potter World with family. Let's just say I was "culture shocked" and we'll leave it at that. As a military vet with a few deployments under my belt, I had a hard time dealing with the hundreds of little fat kids running around in their Harry Potter capes screaming and whining. Not to mention I get a little anxious around large crowds of people. I realized I was in trouble after the first five minutes inside the gate. I did manage to suck it up for the remainder of the day. I'm not a big discount hunter, but was a little disappointed that the military discount was only $3 off a $160 ticket. If you're a yuppy family from the mid west with a couple of spoiled fat kids, then you may enjoy this park. I did not.

We bought two day tickets for Universal parks and what a bust. You are forced to use their locker system on most rides for teens and then getting your things out becomes a huge problem. Locker workers are few and far between. The lockers at the Incredible Hulk work other than that very frustrating. If you have someone that will hod your things while you ride it is worth a visit, otherwise skip this.
The rides were great once you got on but the wait was sometimes hours. I don't think I'll ever go back.

We have been to 3 other Universal Studios but I think this is the worst. First, our family of 4 adults, got a ticket for a two days as advised so we can relax and be at ease no hurries for the rides around the park, one park one day. We chose to park nearer and that is coughing extra $10.00 on top of regular parking (total $35.00) even though we were there when the park opened 9am. At the door, we were offered front of line passes for extra $120.00. But since we thought 9am was early for us to go around and finish the rides, we opted not to. Besides paying $115 for a day ticket + another $120.00 seem ridiculous (total $235.00). Anyway, by 11 am, we finished 3 rides. By the time we got to the Harry Potter area, the lines were very long -- 120 mins. So we just let our teeners line up. My husband and I just decided to go around and wait at some designated area for our children. First I noticed that a lot of structures which I thought were stores turned out to be just facades, a little frustrated. Then after several hours we came to know that our sons had to line up 2 hours at most for each ride. We had no choice but to wait for them. Which made me think that if the waiting for each attraction was two hours, then the park has OVERSOLD ITSELF TO CAPACITY. Why sell that many tickets or allow a lot of people in if the rides cannot even accommodate them. 2 hours and more in line under the heat of the sun most of the time is ridiculous. So what they could have done was sell you $235.00 ticket in the first place. Which at that price I am sure nobody will buy. The marketing guru behind this entity is a genius. First they max out to capacity, then they sell you another ticket to make your life easier. So it is a win-win situation for them and customers end up grumbling. Hey and there's more, some rides require you to have empty pockets and bags be in the locker. Lockers are $3.00 for first 30 minutes. So the longer the lines, the more money you pay for the lockers. See I told you, they are the geniuses! So the next day, my husband and I did not go to the other theme park wasting our tickets (that was our choice though). I was telling my sons get the Front -of-line passes so they do not have the same experience as the day before. But lo and behold. The FOL ticket on that day turned out to be $180.00 per person and only the younger son bought as my older son thought it was just SO RIDICULOUS. So after 6 hours, they were out of the theme park.
