Younger son had 6 rides for $300.00 while the older son held on to his bags not to avoid the locker in some rides. We picked them up and we all swore that we will never go to this theme park again. And I promised to do a write up to make other families aware of our sad experience.

Having time of my life walking around, The Blues Brother concert was a bonus. It's such an amazing place. The kid has a blast riding Transformer and other. Being Harry Potter fan walking to what you see in the movie is so exciting
20 years ago came here loved every minute of it, compared to what it once was this place is now garbage. Rather have a day in Blackpool and that's saying something

Very good day with the family..surprisingly not too much people in Feb. (We had the Fast Lanes pass - but most of the attractions had waiting time 20mnts in average). Attractions were amazing and we really enjoyed the mix of 3Dmovies/roller-coasters. The Harry Potter area is transporting you in another world.

our two sons are 11 and 9 years old. they loved everything. we enjoyed every part, rides and themes from comic strip, super hero, king kong, Jurassic world, harry potter, Sinbad, the simpsons, curious George , etc.

Myself, husband and 2 kids (9 & 11) spent the day at Universal Studios. We stayed the week at Disney and spent 4 days at those parks and 1 day at Universal. Our favorite day was the one spent at Universal. My kids LOVE rides and so this was perfect for them. On the day we planned to visit, I almost backed out because it was supposed to rain all day. It did! But, I think the rain kept a lot of the crowd away, so if you don't mind getting a little wet, then rainy days are perfect! I also purchased the one time express pass for each of my kids so that they could quickly re-ride anything they loved. In my opinion, even when it isn't crazy crowded, the one time express pass was worth the money. My kids also loved Diagon Alley. If I had to chose between universal and islands of adventure, then I would chose Islands of adventure for my family, but we could have easily spent a full day at universal alone and have a great time! We will be back...

This park is so fantastic and gorgeous.....we spent at least 9 hours exploring and walking around. It wasn't too crowded, which is always a plus! The lines for the rides weren't too bad either. There are so many restaurants and food stands to choose from. All the employees are so friendly and helpful.

I love the memories, the older things they have and the newer, to stay up with the times. I am not a big fan of the Simpsons and it is a little gross to me but it is very colorful and I do like the ride, as an adult. I would, however, not allow young children to pay attention to the horrible things you see in the lines. The even enlarged the Simponville area so there are many things to see and do.. Its like a carnival area.  I love the Mummy Ride!!! Rip Ride Rocket is Thrilling!!!! Men in Black is super fun for the whole family. The Minion ride, even though it is thought of, as a child's ride, it is my favorite! It is so adorable and the graphics are amazing! Transformers is super exciting... Shrek is now a classic and fun... There are plenty of places to eat in the park and they even have a starbucks :) My favorite item is the dippin' dots.. though... and if you have small children or a child at heart then you would love Seuss Landing.  The newest addition is the Harry Potter area. It is my absolute favorite and you can never tire of it. The ride is thrilling and their are so many things to do while you are in the Alley. If want some extra fun, get a wand and practice around the park ;)  You can go back over and over again and you never tire of it.

the Harry Potter train between the two parks was fun. The rest of the park was a waste of time and money - all shops and no entertainment. Quite a letdown after experiencing Disney. Universal was crowded, with no place to sit down and take a break.  I recommend saving your money and going elsewhere.
Good park if you arrive early, can be costly as you now have to pay for photos with the charicaters. Food also costly so advise to eat before arrive.

My friend and I came to Orlando for a vacation. We spent 4 days at Disney, which was fabulous! When we got to Universal all we have had is problems. I got double charged for my reservation tickets. We had breakfast reservations at the 3 Broomsticks, I didn't realize that you need to print your reservation ticket but I was told by an extremely rude hostess that was the case. I went to the train station to get them printed out and was told that they couldn't find my reservation even though I had it on my phone in my email from Universal. I have worked in retail so I always try to be nice to others in retail so I know it wasn't me being rude.   I will never come here nor will I ever recommend it without letting someone what I have gone through here. We won't even go back to the park for our last day.  In my opinion, go to Disney!

If you wanted a healthy snack all on offer is a pot of melon only (they call it a fruit cup!) at Starbucks or from a cart in The Harry Potter section. Not as good as Disney as for a healthy lunch,I couldn't even find salad, although it was very busy, so didn't queue for long in a couple of places.
Not impressed. The Harry Potter space was the only part of universal that we enjoyed. In order to see all of the Harry Potter world we had to buy a pass for both parks.
I bought my 4 teenage and we had a great time. Lots of great attractions. We loved the 4d movies. Favorites include Jimmy Fallon, minions, & the make up show.

I have never been so bored at a theme park in my life. Legoland is more entertaining because my kids actually have fun. Half of the rides are old and irrelevant to our pop culture these days. No one watches ET, The Mummy, Terminator, Shrek or Fear Factor. I don't even know many people who still love the Simpsons. Transformers ride is okay, its identical to Spider-Man, just not Spider-Man. The rest of the rides are just all the same. And not work the wait at all. Jimmy Fallon is fun because it's him and its NY. But all of the rides, even that one, do not have clear pictures. Everything is blurry, like im watching tv on my old tv from the 90s. I would think the technology is there to create crystal clear pictures and lifelike experiences now especially since we have crystal clear pictures on our Tvs. The kids area was fun. Loved curious George. I'm not sure why Barney is still there. Barney is old. Most kids are watching Paw Patrol...which is Nickelodeon and I dont get why the only Nickelodeon characters there are Spongebob. Even he's a tad old. My poor preschooler only met Bart and Homer characters LOL and he still was happy about it but seriously...come on people. This park could be so great. But there is just lack of imagination and no trying to keep up with the times. Why not have a Batman ride? Super man? Those never go out of style. Harry Potter is cool, but again, not work the money. I felt like I was just walking around looking at teeny stores and fake stores that I wanted to go into but couldn't. I couldn't even ride the ride because the line was just too long.

For $110, you'd think that Universal would at least include all the Harry Potter attractions in one park. But nooooo. I knew in advance that because the Hogwarts Express stops in the other park you had to buy a multi-park pass to ride it, but what I didn't know was that THREE of the other four Harry Potter rides are in the other park, even the Hogwarts one. All you get in the Wizarding World is the Gringotts ride and a bunch of overpriced shops. At least the frozen butterbeer was good. And no, I didn't buy a wand. I wasn't going to spend $45 ($50 if you want an interactive one) after finding out the "complete" HP experience would have set me back another $55.

Absolutely loved universal studios. My favourite park in Orlando. Crowds weren't half as bad as Disney, the longest we waited for a ride was 20 minutes (escape from gringotts, amazing) my all time favourite ride The Mummy was still as fab as I remembered too! Our little boy loved woody woodpeckers coaster, he managed at least 5 rides everyone we visited and walked on every time. We shared a big pink donut between 5 of us, very reasonable price at only $4.99! Expected to pay around $12 for it. We took a subway lunch in the park with us to save money but meal deals were between $10 and $15. We also requested free iced water from any kiosks that do soda fountain drinks and just added our own squeezy squash rather than paying $3.50 per drink. Can't wait to return!

We went here for my daughters high school graduation vacation. She loves Harry Potter. We had lots of fun. I like using the AP that tells what the wait times are it is very helpful. May is a good time to go before everyone gets out of school and vacations start happening lines where not real bad.

The park was nice, staff ok, the lines are insane and their "express pass" is a scam for everyone that doesn't have one, unless you want to wait in line forever and have the wait time magically change due to people with express pass re-riding without any wait, you should buy a pass. We didn't and ended up not going on many of the rides. Didn't matter as we were there mainly for Harry Potter, where express pass is not accepted. If you don't care about Harry Potter, than I am not sure why you would ever visit these parks. Volcano Bay was nice, but again useless without express pass, 110 min wait that never got any shorter for many of the slides. The attendant told me it was because we didn't have express pass, I was like these tickets weren't free. Anyway, I am rambling. Harry Potter was well done, but crowded and the food at three broom sticks was better than leaky cauldron imo. If your kids are Harry Potter maniacs like mine, worth it, but probably only really need two days, otherwise save your money.
You must purchase tickets for both Universal Studios, Florida and Islands of Adventure to get the whole 'Harry Potter' experience! Do not hesitate, as both locations are worth the experience!

My wife has never been to a theme park. This was her first. We had a great time. Rode all of the rides and saw a few of the shows. For older people, it was like we were kids again. Her smile was worth the whole drive from Savannah. Time to go to the hotel and grab a quick rest before dinner tonight at Capone's.

We took our family to Orlando for Christmas. Some of the older kids wanted to go to Universal. We paid the inflated fee for both sides of the park so they could see all of Harry Potter. That is all we got to see. There was no way we could get on any rides as the wait lines were hours. Don't go there. At least at Disney you can get a fast pass to see your favorite picks and not have to pay extra like at Universal.

Last visited in August 2014 and thought it was ok then. When you compare this to Islands of Adventure there is no comparison . Universal has a few food rides such as Harry Potter and The Mummy but the place needs updating . Rides such as ET and Shrek need getting rid or and replacing !  The parade was poor and lacked any imagination. If you have a choice head to Islands of Adventure!!

We finally went to Universal after putting it off year after year to go somewhere else. Why did we wait so long! This was the best vacation ever. We stayed at Loews Royal Pacific Resort and got the free fast passes which was well worth it. We got the park to park tickets with a meal plan and unlimited drinks which was well worth it in the 97 degree heat. We are already planning our trip to come back next year!

Do yourself a favor and stay on property if you can to get the unlimited express passes. It made the experience a million times better. My son and I rode everything as many times as we wanted without having to worry about the lines.

My daughter had been looking forward to our Florida holiday for a year and we asked her, where would you like to go when we are there?  Of course, you can't go to Florida without going to a theme park. So she picked Universal and I thought "well you can't go wrong with that"  Let's begin.....  You start off with being offered 2 prices for parking. $20 for everyday I would of said or $30 for what would be nearer to the park. We should the expensive one. It is a walk away from the park, quite a walk away so for anyone picking the cheaper price I suggest you buy very comfortable shoes and limber up for months before you travel.  My husband bought 3 tickets, for him, me and our daughter. The queue for tickets was actually ok but the price was a joke. 2 parks for 1 day for 3 people is £600 + and we wanted the expressed ones as I can't stand for too long as I have a fractured knee and back problem. Thought getting the expressed tickets would save us alot of time in queues.  My daughter and husband went on some rides as I watched the Blues Brothers and Marilyn Monroe go round in their cars. I enjoyed that and took some lovely photos.  We took drinks in with us and this is a MUST for anyone on goes to Universal. I saw Hello Kitty, or should I say someone in a costume with a park official going around with them. There was also a group of people clearly doing a VIP trip. Park officials with them, carrying bags on pushy trolleys and having photos with the minions. What I didn't expect as I sat on a wall and witnessed was a young mum who wanted her daughter to have her photo with a minion and then being TD by official staff that no photos could be taken and that she should stand away from where they are. I couldn't believe it, because a group of people who clearly have more money than sense paid more for their tickets they and them alone are the only worthy people of getting photos with the characters. The mum was not happy and the little girl was crying.  My husband and daughter started off on the Shrek ride and then the minion ride. Both weren't traditional rides but sit down cinema like journeys where the seats moved. Daughter liked it, husband thought it Shrek was boring but minion was good.  What makes you wonder in this theme park are the things you don't see unless you look for them. There are a splattering of rides and alot of no nothing parts to this park. Done superbly but still no nothing. A New York part, a LA part that kind of thing, you get the idea. What they are are sets where you think things are but aren't. Dummy shops, fabulous in their looks and great photos to be taken but a substantial part of a walkway before you get to eating places which are more than expensive.  We went into a burger restaurant, ordered 3 "big ones" and a drink to go with it. Had to queue for a while to be served then another queue to pick up the item. No sauces or ketchups were offered and I couldn't even see one of those stations with napkins etc either. I put my cup underneath for a drink and there was a lot of drinks on offer so the choice was quite extensive. It was over 100 degrees the day we went and with very few places in the shade you need to be hydrated. The price of 3 burgers and a drink was over 40 dollars and the drink wasn't even refillable. Now that is a joke!  Going through the park there are some great eye catchers but my daughter wanted to see Harry Potter and we all excited to go on the Hogwarts express train. Finally, getting to the front of the queue and we got our tickets out. Only 2 of our tickets were expressed and my one wasn't. I was told there was a 20 minute wait for the other queue and told my husband "you 2 go and meet me back here when your finished" but Shania who worked there was lovely enough to see me go through as a family. The train did not disappoint and was a highlight for Universal. Clearly done and lots to see the journey from 1 park to another was great. I unfortunately couldn't and didn't go on anything as my ticket wasn't expressed and I can't wait in a queue as some rides were over 75 minutes to wait for. I sat and watched my daughter enjoy herself and that was the focus of all of this. Afterwards we go back on the Hogwarts express train and back to the original park after their enjoyment. I sat on yet another wall watching the attractions around me whilst my family went on The Simpsons rides and after being fleeced for 5 dollars for a bottle of water my daughter had a slushy drink for another 5 dollars. Over 50 dollars on food and drink, well a steamrollered burger and drinks shared amongst 3 of us was quite excessive at over 50 dollars.  10 and a half hours later my back is unbearable and we started to make our way back to the car. My husband wanted to talk to someone at customer services or what they call "guest services" but this is right at the front of where you come in so if your grievance is further in the park you'll have further to go to simply talk to someone  The young girl at the desk seemed a little unsure of our circumstances and went to talk to a supervisor 4 times before the supervisor finally came out to talk to us.  We told her we bought 3 tickets and only 2 of them were expressed. I couldn't go on any rides because they refused me entry in the expressed lanes even though my husband and daughter had their passes. I got on the Hogwarts train ONLY because of the niceness of Shania and was then told " sorry we won't refund you your ticket because everyone has to pay something to get into the park" yes they do. To simply walk through their turnstiles it's $140, can you believe that. We were told by this supervisor that I should of got a wheelchair if I wasn't able to stand. I can stand, I am not disabled but then again no one told us about the wheelchairs either. After a long and lengthy battle she offered me 3 expressed park tickets for another day even though I told her over and over and over again I was going home in a couple of days and I couldn't come back again. I was then offered $100 gift card for a dinner so I could have time with my family. Told her I didn't come to Universal for a dinner and then she offered us to refund the expressed parts of the other 2 tickets which was over £200.  She then gave me my original ticket back plus 2 ordinary tickets for my daughter and husband and told us "you have 3 tickets now if you want to go back into the park"  Does anyone at Universal listen? Other good people complaining it's a joke. Universal make millions of dollars everyday and they don't listen to what the very people who make them billionaires say to them  Our experience was a joke and I wouldn't go back again  Overpriced over hyped day out that costs a fortune and no one listens to you. That sentence alone sums up our experience of the day

Visited Universal Studios Halloween Horror night on 17th Sept. A really good evening at the park. Didn't manage to see everything in the one night even though the queues wasn't that long, maximum one was roughly 30mins. The Horror Studios were very good with some brill actors. Quite a lot of walking so comfy shoes needed. A few of the rides were shut were closed for evening maintenance but it wasn't a problem. Staff was helpful and you need a map to pick the bits you want to see.

We visited in September and managed to go to the first 3 Halloween Horror Nights - we really loved this, lots of scares, plenty to see and lots of rides such as the Mummy and Rip Ride Rocket stay open. We would definitely recommend but not for the faint hearted !. Great fun 😀
Would never advise anyone to deal with the reservations staff, probably contracted, and totally unreliable.

Very disappointed by my recent visit to your horror night event, clearly a case of profit over guest satisfaction. You had obviously issued too many tickets for the event which resulted in a very poor experience in the park, horror houses were basically one big line of people meaning there was no scare factor to them as you could see what was coming as it happened to the guests in front, express pass was a complete rip off as you still had to wait over 30 minutes in line for each of the attractions. Cast member were miserable and clearly not interested in being there. Not the experience I would have hoped for having spent $1000 for 5 of us to attend. Guest services on the night were not interested in dealing with complaints.

2 weeks in Florida and it was the only park we wanted to do twice! It's absolutely amazing, awesome and we had a ball there. Queuing was easy we went early both days and did every ride with only a 5 minutes wait, Hogwarts is unbelievable, the express train was fantastic taking us to Hogsmeade, the rides were totally brilliant were big HP fans and the attention to detail in both parks was just fantastic. Our son is 7 and was so disappointed at Magic Kingdom but absolutely thrilled to bits with Universal we were totally chilled enjoyed every second of both days. Hulk, Spider-Man, Kong, return of the mummy and Transformers all amazing rides, Dr Doom was untrue, Fantastic park worth every penny.

Any trip to universal Orlando is always a great time we had such a great time from the moment we stepped foot there. The entertainment is excellent and the food my god so many great places to eat. I love the food the resturants are awesome city walk is great just a good time all the time can't wait to go back in 2018 😀

Loved this park. Harry Potter area amazing. Every detail is special for all fans. Ride train. Mummy ride was actually one of our favorites there. Lots of different areas for all ages. My only complaint of both parks is how 4D has taken over. Way too many nauseous glasses wearing rides.

We have been to Disneyland several times and have always enjoyed our experience with our children, however upon learning about Ollivanders at Harry Potter we were intrigued by it, after an hour wait we thought it was going to be worth it with good reviews about the experience, however it would have to be the worst time wasting experience ever- unless your a Harry Potter fanatic and even then it would surely disappoint many. Upon entry you are greeted by a lady who talks a few words about wands, then thinking we might be entering into an exciting room we are taken into the gift shop and that was it. I could not believe it. I won’t ever get my wasted one hour waiting in line again but unless you have time to spare this is a complete disappointment to Disney.

This is the first time we had been back to Orlando for 9 years and it was a nightmare. They advertise as where dreams come true Orlando must change it too where queues come true. Disney,Universal and Sea world attractions have got it all wrong now with charging for car parking which you can now pay for VIP parking from an average 20 dollars to 40 dollars on top of the park entry ticket cost which has you waiting at the entry booths for up to an hour this is before you get into the parks. This is an average day at the parks there were two families of us and we tried to get too the parks about 09.00 and so did everybody else. When you do get to the park gates the first hurdle is the bag search that can also take up to an hour to get through them as there is not enough bag search people working. When through this another queue to get your fingerprint and photo taken for your pass so you cannot pass on to anybody else eventually get into the park 10.30. The fast pass carry on was not fully described to us on our first day and this is another shambles these must be booked prior to you coming to the park on the app or computer disney link to give you any chance of getting on any of the rides. The fast pass fiasco only gives you 3 rides that you can get early access too or you have to take your chance and sit in the queues which has now got out of hand letting too many people in to the parks with most rides over 200 mins to wait for. Disney and Universal have put profit before enjoyment waiting in excess of 3 hours for a 2 min ride is a farce. Be warned if you go at a busy time of the year you need to book rides before you go to the parks. Universal is the worst with the quick queue pass which was at 159 dollars each on top of your entry ticket and parking charge allowing you to half the queue times which was also a sham. Harry Potter,Kong,Spiderman and Hulk rides all over 200 mins when we arrived at the park a few were off due to the bad weather which adds to the misery. This is what you can expect on a normal day.  Most popular ride 200 mins waiting time which is around 3 hours for a 2 min ride is totally unacceptable and why should people pay over and above the admission ticket too still queue for over an hour too many people allowed into the parks during xmas and new year management have got it all wrong and we will certainly not be back to Orlando Parks again. The whole experience of Disney and Universal has lost its way to money grabbing profit and do not cater for the punter now a rip off.

We have had it with theme parks. We had some bad experiences with regard to excessive crowd sizes/wait times at parks in some other states, but we thought A world-class resort like Orlando Studio's would have figured out how to mitigate that somehow, right? Nope.  There was the 385 minute wait to ride the hulk coaster...over 6 hours...seriously? The shortest line during our 2 day visit was 30 minutes for E.T., which is an old, obsolete attraction that did not impress.  We did "pre-register for Jimmy Fallon's New York ride, which was awesome. We registered upon arrival, were given a time to return, and then the line was actually enjoyable based on the live entertainment, the video entertainment and so forth. The ride itself, while short, was excellent.  However, we only rode on 3 ride in 2 days, plus observed a live performance of "Fear Factor".  Universal Studios: Here's a thought....raise your ticket prices so that you reduce the load in the park while still maintaining revenues. Maybe if you double your entrance fee you'd cut your load in half?  Also, hire a flow analysis engineer to figure out ways to relieve bottlenecks at the attractions. Perhaps the Jimmy Fallon ride is a glimpse at the future?  Otherwise we enjoyed walking through the park, it really is a cool place. Was it worth $800 to do so? No.

Loved our time at Universal. We had a 3 day park to park ticket which was great, as we went during the busy period. Our first few days were just after New Years. So still crazy busy. We did not have fast passes, so had to wait. Some wait times were 90-120 mins. Sometimes we went single rider. At times it was faster but at some rides it was slower. The first two days we went first to Universal then the second day Islands of Adventure. Didn't utilize the park to park. Our 3rd day was on Monday Jan the 8th. Weather was nice park was not so busy, wait times were short early in day which we took advantage of. We went to both parks that day. So much to see and do. Rides are amazing the whole atmosphere and buildings they are in like Harry Potter and King Kong so realistic. Harry Potter worlds were great. Loved the frozen butter beer. My Favourite ride was Hulk. Thought both parks were nice and colourful.

We had a great time however a few observations which we shared with customer services but they did not seem to be that bothered ( they replied , forwarded my comments to the management team but they did not take the time to respond )  The breakfast was nice just a shame on a “VIP Experience “that it was served with budget plastic plates, knives, forks and disposable coffee cups.  We were advised to arrive 45 minutes early , then booked to start the tour at 9.30 – We arrived at the E.T ride for 9.30 but the ride does not open until 10.00.  At the E.T ride , The lady in the gift shop advised Emily our tour guide , we could wait inside in the waiting area inside next to the film memorabilia , to allow Emily to pass the waiting time talking to us about various trivia but after a few minutes inside the operating staff rather rudely advised us we were not allowed to wait inside so we had to stand outside.  It was poor enough on a VIP tour having to wait 30 minutes never mind outside twiddling pour thumbs  Our tour guide suggested we had 90 minutes lunch, we were here to see the park back stage not sit on our backsides – 45 minutes was ample.    Emily was a good guide, totally versed on all the background information on the rides we visited but I would have liked to hear about more park trivia than we did. Too many quiet times on our tour, I had to pump for information on number visitors a day , number of staff.  Finishing at 4.00, the attractions we visited / rode were good but we could have seen so much more.  We were a little restricted as we were paired up with a family with young children ( our daughter is 13 ) so Cat in the Hat and a few others not really of interest  Finally after spending over $1200 on the day for 3 of us , a feedback form or review would have been expected as opposed to having to mail direct …Yours A un-gratified customer !

We went for the Celebration of Harry Potter and had an amazing time! But there’s so much more to do at the park! It’s family friendly and there’s something to do here for everyone, young or old! Clean, well organized and staff is very helpful and friendly! We will definitely be returning for another visit!
Thought our teen would go directly to Harry Potter, but he didn't. In fact, we didn't make it there until the next day! Great family fun for everyone. Absolutely as good as Disney!

Hey! So I was really excited for Universal for my birthday, they gave me a button and everyone was saying happy birthday. That part was really cool..  UNFORTUNATELY I had not been in a while and every ride is a 3D simulation ride now. I dont like the 3D simulation rides at all - esp one after another they make me disoriented and nauseous. I go to theme parks for coasters and thrills! Unfortunately, there are no coasters left between two parks except Hulk - That's right ONE roller coaster. between TWO parks (There is the mummy which is a small indoor coaster if you count little ones.)  Basically, this place is to walk around as a novelty; cute shops and decor. It's great for children especially if they like 3D rides and not actual moving rides. For teens and adults this place is a major bust. You can grab a coffee and hang out, if you want thrills you wont find them here. They tore down the dueling dragons, the best coasters they had. There just isn't anything left at this point except one coaster the Hulk which gave me whiplash really bad.  BUSCH GARDENS is really where it's at for thrills. They have a ton of coasters and they are ultra smooth and never give you whiplash especially Montu and Sheikra my two favorite coasters. Bush Gardens is MUCH better for couples, teens, and adults. If you like actual rides that move and not just simulation cop-out bs then just go to Busch Gardens - Universal sold out.

Universal really has grown since the last time I've visited. Most everyone we encountered who works there, was friendly, informative, and outgoing. Diagon Alley is great, and should be visited first thing in the morning. Some attractions can be skipped (like Race Through New York Starring Jimmy Fallon). Saw the Mardi Gras parade which was surprisingly good. Having Universal Express would have been nice, so I recommend staying at an on-site hotel that includes that.

It's a great place with interesting rides and attractions. Wait times for rides can be long on certain rides but lines continuously move. I like how they incorporate the 'ride theme' in all the rides so you have something to look at while waiting in line, it's really smart. That Harry Potter area is really cool. I liked The Mummy indoor coaster ride it was so fun. That Rip Ride Rocket coaster... it took me all day to get the courage to go on it, it really is something. Service from all staff really good - Americans get it right when it comes to customer service. There are areas/rides in the park that are dated which should be replaced like MiB and Simpsons, did not like these very much. Overall I had a great time, but I liked Island of Adventure better.

Must stay to see parade and get some beads!!!my favorite universal activity is islands of adventure the Harry potter ride!!! Best ride ever and don't forget to get butter beer a butterscotch slurpee or frozen ice worth every penny of 8 to 12$ depending on size!!!

I had never been to the parks before, as I was a Disney fan. However, the Park was amazing. The Simpson area was wonderful, the rides were great, and the only issue we had is that we didn’t get to ride the Transformers ride because it was closed due to an issue. But that was just us not wanting to wait for it to fix. The staff was mostly interested in talking with each other and several times there were supervisors chastising them to interact with the guests. That didn’t bother me though, so it still gets full stars from me!
The park is a joke and their guest service is even worse! Go to disney! Dont waste your money here. This is a waste of time and energy

If you have recently visited Disney, you may be disappointed with this park. For the cost and crowds, you will get a much better value at Disney. We paid $149 above the ticket price we paid for an express pass unlimited. This should have decreased wait times considerably, but apparently the number of passes sold is not limited. We still had to wait over an hour for the Harry Potter ride even with the express pass unlimited. Also, we stayed in a Universal resort and still had to pay to park at the resort. The only benefit to staying at the resort was a shuttle to the parks, and an extra hour at Harry Potter, which we were not big fans so it was not a big draw for us. Also, communication is poor; it was difficult to try and figure out how everything worked with the crowds, which the park cannot handle very well.The rules for what you can and cannot wear/take on rides is very inconsistent. For example, I was made to put my cell phone in a locker for a ride, yet 4 people in front of me had phones and were taking pictures throughout the line. This was our first trip to Universal Studios since 2005 and we missed many of the themed movie rides and demonstrations and shows they had at Universal Studios. Also, you can cover the park in a day...not a lot to do.The food is very expensive and all our meals were cold, hamburgers/fries were not even warm. Keep expectations low when visiting! Next time, we will probably go back to Disney.

I was there with my 9 year old daughter and wife for Spring Break. Prior to going, I told my daughter how magical this place was. I told her how you get to ride the movies and be a part of the movies. When we arrived, we were all very disappointed to find that most of the classic rides that made Universal famous, were gone. Now, every ride is simply a 3-d simulator. We went to ride the movies, not sit down and watch movies. Even my daughter was not impressed by the simulators. She watched videos of earthquake, jaws, king kong, twister.......it's shameful what has been done to this once amazing park. Disney has maintained its classic rides and added new ones.

Universal studios, Orlando presents a relaxed fun experience. During our visit we were able to ride on every attraction with less than a 15 minute wait. The only ride we choose not to ride was the roller coaster. The staff were very helpful when we asked questions about a particular attraction. We enjoyed a delicious lunch at Fisherman’s Wharf. The only negative factor in the pricing was the excessive fee to purchase an express pass. The high fees for parking, entrance and express pass make it very difficult for people with limited income to enjoy this facility.

After all the hype of the new ride. This was the one I had to ride obviating the year. For a new ride the stand by line was only 30 minutes. The Pre Ride display is cheap and liked more like a military surplus than what was suppofilmsed to be a garage. Al the cars are shadow copies not an original screen car to be seen. And even these seemed to be of poor quality. The the pre show which while entertaining only showed how cheaply this ride had been thrown together. All the performance of the live and recorded “film actors” was more wooden than Pinocchio on shrek4d. Obviously all shot separately and then edited together. Then onto the ride built to do only one thing get as many through the ride as possible. The “buses” were filled 5 wide so the person in the middle have a very poor view. The party scene was classic F&F . Then. More wooden acting. And what has to be the shortest and most ridiculously fashioned chase scene. In conclusions poor ride for one of the longest running film franchises. It was almost like the theme parks are mocking the movies. In comparison the “Back to the future” ride was far better when that was released all those years ago. You would have thought with a decade on of technological updates. It would have pushed the interactive envelope further.

From the parking, to the gate and with locker rentals, it's a mess. Super long wait times and the rides close if it rains even a bit. Lots of in park carnival games (that cost). Not impressed and won't be back.

What ever you do avoid the fast and furious ride. Without doubt the worst ride I have ever ridden. The que was more exciting than the ride. Biggest waste of time. I waited for this ride for 3 years when I first visited and I'm so disappointed

My wife and I have older children and had the chance to visit both of the parks while in Florida. We decided to make it a fun for just the 2 of us. I enjoy the City Walk area and the energy of the parks. While I enjoyed the great rides and experiences I could help but leave extremely disappointed in the lack of service and general lack of concern for the guest experience. This is one area Disney cannot be beat. From the painfully slow and disorganized line to get our tickets to the disinterested wait staff at the restaurants in the park, It made it a poor experience. The line to get our tickets took about an hour. When we finally got to the window it closed for the worker to go on break. We waited again for the window to be reopened. At multiple times we stopped to get food or drinks. It was rare anyone made eye contact with the customer or (for most interactions) didn't even stop there conversation with their coworker. Money was just taken and change placed on the counter without stopping a sentence. The crowning failure was when a worker on a Harry Potter ride pulled us out of line rudely because my wife had a small purse worn cross body. He ignored the families in from and behind us that had diaper bags and back packs, and rudely directed my wife to the lockers and then sternly walked me out of the line area (like a 3 year old) and told me to stay there until my wife got back. I asked for his name and he said Noah. When I repeated it back to him he said Noel. I guessed he was lying about his name. When I questioned him about pulling us out of line like he did he got very upset, raised his voice and yelled "DO YOU WANT TO SEE MY MANAGER". I remained calm and told him how he was acting I would handle it through Customer Service. After going back and forth with him yelling, another worker came up (I assume it was his manager). He screamed in front of everyone “this guy wants to talk to you.” By this point my wife returned. I told the other person that I would deal with this later. Noel/Noah stood in front of me and would not let us rejoin the line and repeated that we wanted to talk with the manager. I repeated my statement and had to physically shoulder by Noel/Noah for us to get back in line.  I tried to let it go, but finally decided to us the customer service link and sent an email regarding my experience since we spent the extra $125 per ticket for the express pass. In my complaint I asked for the money back for the express pass if their staff can just pull us at will. The week following out trip I get a voicemail that customer service reviewed my complaint and since I had used my express pass multiple times that day I obviously had enjoyed the pass so she would not refund my money. She said if I called her back we might be able to “work something out”.  If you are looking for great customer service, this is NOT the place to visit.

So I read different reviews about this ride. I even read that is was a party bus and somewhat like the king Kong ride. While I thought it would be better to be in cars for the ride I said "well how bad can it be?" First you use your fast pass and somehow get shoved in together with all the other riders. No separate line anywhere. You walk through the garage and all that stuff is neat to look at. You end up being herded like cows with no lines and no organization at all. Then yes you are placed on a bus and the action starts. It seems pretty cool and just when its getting good, the ride ends. It just ends. And your left there thinking "what just happened?' The One guy I think Jamie was his name was super awesome and fully. He was the best part of the whole thing. Unless they improve this ride it really is a waste of time. Suggestion, walk through and see all the good stuff then find and exit.

We were quoted in Canadian prices when we booked through Universal. Get my visa a week later and I was charged in u.s dollars. Which made a difference of $ 845.00. I called to complain and they said no we don't have any Canadian prices on our website. all of our prices are in U.S funds. Look again!!!  Spoke to supervisor and she listened to the recording and said that the representative did not quote me in Canadian dollars. I asked to hear the recording as I wrote down everything I was quoted word for word and then asked to speak to another supervisor.  they reviewed the tape again and yes of course they did hear i was quoted in Canadian Dollars. I would not recommend booking through Universal studios and where ever you do book get the agents name, and make sure you repeat everything bAck to the agent clearly so just in case its reviewed you are covered.

I just priced tickets for the upcoming 2018 horror nights and it looks like its going to cost us 1456.00 to attend the park during the day, then go to horror nights in the evening. Seems like a rip-off to charge 170 for a shorter day and staying in an onsite hotel does not help because you have to by a separate fast pass for the evening? There should be some kind of break for a full day good lord, forget it

I must say that this has to be the worst ride I've ever been on! I would've been completely upset if I had to wait in line for it. Fortunately when we tried to download the app for a time to return, it wouldn't work, so one of the staff just took us straight on the ride. And let me tell you, what a letdown! It was super short and absolutely ridiculous. Stick to transformers and even the jimmy fallon ride thru new york and please bypass this time waster.

Went with my 13 yr old son last week. Both parks are good with a few really good coasters and thrill rides. Some of the areas are starting to seem dated however such as the ET ride. We were there 3 days but you could do it all in 2 or even 1 with a park hopper ticket and express passes.

For one adult and one child it was 258 for us to get in. To wait in lines that we’re 65 minutes long for rides-we opted out of that. So we walked around looking for other interesting things to do and there really was nothing but a bunch of shops to spend your money. Or buy god and sweets. Or play fair like games that costs money. Just be prepared to wait in long lines or to spend money to get in to spend more money to feel like you’ve had a good time. We won’t be back at least with Disney there’s a ton of shows and parades and character experiences we were there for seven hours and only seen spongebob twice.
I don't ride a lot of rides, but I thoroughly enjoyed wandering around the park. I had never been to Universal Studios before. I am so glad I took time out of this vacation to spend 2 days there!

We came here mainly for the harry potter area and were not disappointed the detail and theming are amazing the frontiers ride is the best harry potter ride. The shops in diagon alley are amazing as is the butterbeer, we spent a lot in the shops so bring a lot of money. We also liked the Hollywood rocket and mummy rides, top tip get here for opening as the lines become quickly huge and express pass is a lot of money on top of your tickets and not free like disney, so wait times were up to 100mins.

We had a lovely holiday in Universal with our ten year old son. We spent 7 days at Universal, and filled everyday. Our favourite family rides were Men in Black ( shooting game like buzz light year one), Harry Potter Escape from GrinGoths and ET. The Harry Potter areas were very good, at the start of the day the park was not busy, and we never had to wait to get into these areas. The Harry train was extremely good and different in each direction. We stayed in one of the onsite hotels (Royal Pacific) which meant an extra hour, hoverever there were only a few rides open In this time, a good time to do Harry Potter. The hotel meant you got free express passes, so worth considering. 10 minute flat walk to Universal or a boat. The drink refill mug was worth doing, $14 day one the $8 to refill after. Lots of choices on drinks at refill stations. With a ten year old we personally preferred it to Disney but our son was tall enough to do all the rides. His favourite thrill rides were Hollywood Rocket and Hulk. I also enjoyed The Cat in the Hat area, although childish, fun!

Our ten year old son had an amazing day here. Best ride Rockin but the Harry Potter Diagon Alley is fab you could spend a day in there especially if you purchase an interactive wand like we did. On the downside the characters costumes could do with a wash they look scruffy compared to a local popular park with mice...... 😜

We have been to both Universal and Disney recently, and if you are trying to decide between the two I would suggest Disney. I feel they nickel and dime you at Universal, where at Disney once you are in you really don't have to pay extra for anything. Disney's fast passes are great...universal's not so much. Disney has five parks which is a ton to see. Universal does have good rides, and Harry Potter World, but Disney still gets my vote every time.
Terrible. The best past was seeing the cars in the que. Don't bother going on it. You are in a bus like the Kong ride. Not thrilling in the least. It's actually silly.

I had a blast. I wish some of the old rides were still in the park (like Jaws). I had a great time. The park was very clean. I didn't have to wait more than 15 mins for any ride. I was able to ride everything at least twice. I will be back.

This review is ONLY regarding the HHN 2018 production. After attending opening weekend, I am extremely dissapointed in the technology and support systems Universal has in place for this event. From the manual entering of id codes that slowed the entry gates, to the incredibly outdated photo pass system, I can't help but wonder why this gets so much hype. The scare zones were lame and predictable. Hay monsters??? Really? Stranger Things was very well done, and its too bad they can't manage the crowd for this event better. You shouldn't have to pay an extra $100 for an express pass to avoid wasting 90-120 minutes in line. Take a lesson from Disney and figure out how to allow patrons to enjoy other parts of the park while waiting for their turn to experience your main attraction. On our second night, we arrived at 5:15 thinking we were plenty early, but didn't get through the gates til 6:40. we went straight to stragner things because it was a 120 minute wait the night before at 11pm. We got out of Stranger Things at 8:45 and left the park exhausted from standing in line with no water or drinks. The only picture we got as a group also cut my daughter off. Thanks for the memories...

People who are giving this park a good review must of had combo tickets or just don't know what a good park should consist of! $125.00 for LITERALLY about 12 RIDES is shameful! I felt sorry for my son, but he was a trooper and didn't really complain concerning the lack of rides at this money grabbing park!

Do not go at 9 am. Everyone is in a hurry to be first in long lines. Instant 45 minute waits. Not good for mobility challenged individuals. From one end to another it is food and stores. All rides except the train come with warnings that exclude a large number of people over 60. We ate at 3 Broomsticks. The fries were okay, but the fish tasted oily and was cold by the time we got to a table (with very low chairs). I paid $1500 Canadian for 4 x 2 day, park hopper passes, and after 4 hrs we were at the exit and will not be returning for a second day. What a waste of money!!!!. You get nothing for your entry fee. Go to Disney instead, where there is street entertainment everywhere, so much more fun.

Good selection of rides and not so crowded as Disney.  We have visited several times over the years, and agree with most reviewers that this is a good attraction.  However, there is one issue that has not been resolved since it opened and visitors should be aware of. I can see that this has been mentioned by other visitors in the past within reviews.  The journey from the entrance of the Mummy ride, to the ride itself has varying levels of lighting, of which some is too low for many people to have a clear view of the way forward. One of the worst areas is just before you get on the ride, where there is a flight of metal steps. The bottom two steps had no lighting. My wife tripped and fell, bruising her leg. I also tripped behind her. My wife has difficulty walking the rest of the day due to the bruising. This was reported to Guest Services.  I should also add that we had a similar problem in Skull Kingdom in IOA.

My husband and I had fun time at the Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure parks. For the two of us, our favorite part was the Universal Studios, we went on way more rides there. The only one that was a huge let down was the Fast and Furious one, there was a lot of build up, but it very short and not very thrilling. The end of the MIB ride was a let down, but had the potential to be a lot of fun. I wish more rides were interactive like that one. I'm a Harry Potter fan so I enjoyed the rides at both parks and the immersive experience at the Universal Studios Park. Would recommend for people to go.
We had a great time. The park is well done. The fountain light show at the end of the night is good. The lines were short when we were there. Most were under 15 minutes.

It's easy to get caught up in all the fantastic experiences at Universal studios! This is my family's second trip, coming down from Massachusetts. This trip the parks were much busier, which is totally understandable being Christmas vacation week. Aside from long lines for food and some drink stands things were great. I would totally recommend staying at one of the onsite hotels to get the unlimited express pass. Wasting time in lines is no fun! Totally worth the extra $$ Also we got to meet plenty of characters. Beetle juice was my favorite

As much as the rides were thrilling and some were really awesome, be prepared to queue up to 3 hours for the popular rides. Most rides will also be at least an hour or so. Express Pass may be the solution but since there were 5 of us, it would have doubled the cost.  Probably it was due to the peak holiday season but I still felt the waiting time was too long. We bought the 3 days, park to park tickets so we can ride on the Hogwarts Express and take our time but we really struggled.  Queue for food can also go up to 30 mins even not during meal times. Staff looked tired and some were no longer friendly...  It was so crowded in Diagon Alley that stopping to take photos or getting inside the shops became difficult cause of the traffic.  Overall was a poor experience this time at Universal Studio Orlando.

We were there Dec 26 to Dec 29 three day park to park, Harry Potter Forbidden Journey and Escape from Gringotts are both fantastic experience, but you need to get up very early to be there otherwise waiting line can be up to 300 mins, 180 mins is normal waiting time if you get there after 10 AM. So please use advantage of your early admission if you have. We found that two roller coasters Hulk and Rocket are a little less popular than KingKong or Minion, so after finishing the Harry Potter experience, you can take your Kingkong or Minion before the roller coasters. Also, after 8PM which is the Parade started happening, the coasters can be less people, you can rush to there for your second time. Here is the general suggestions from our three days trip, hope can help you guys. Also, the employees in Universal are very professional and dedicated. They are very good at organizing the long line. Thank you guys. Last tip is download the app Universal from your google store or apple. You can reverse your virtual line, check waiting time and even order food etc. from the app.

We visited on 12/27, family of 14. We purchased Express Passes in the uk before arriving. When we arrived at the park we were sent to 3 different queues - everyone said there had been a problem recognising the passes the day before but no one was able to sort the problem very quickly. Having spent a lot of money to buy the passes we were kept waiting over an hour before they finally issued our passes. This lost us valuable time in the park and the world of Harry Potter was impossible to access by then. It was far from an express service and contrasted sharply with our experience at Aquatica where they had a problem with accessing there cabana bookings and just said ‘go through and enjoy the park and we can sort out payment later’. Even with the express pass we were denied access to some rides in the World of Harry Potter as we were told the queues were too long to let us in. The fast pass system at Disney is so much better!

First let me say i really enjoy most of the rides at Universal Orlando. Rip Ride, The mummy, transformers, escape Grigots and others are all very well done. But my recent experience on Fast amd Furious was awful. Found it to lack imagination amd i felt that it was an attempt to utilize the kong technology in a way that really doesnt work.  In my opinion i would say that it woukd have been better to combine the budget of Jimmy falon and fast furious into 1 outstanding experience rather then 2 separate mediocre rides.  Really was a let down!!

Spent most of the day at Universal Studies in Orlando today. Must say it was horribly disappointing. Where Disney parks have charm, whimsy and seamless operations, Universal seems to delight in extracting maximum money for minimal entertainment. Even Harry Potter worlds, while lovely in their authenticity to the books, left me cold with their endless merchandising. Worse yet, Universal seems to think that moving platforms and 3D screens are an adequate replacement for real roller coasters. What a let down!

Had one day to visit Universal. Huge fans. Then get up to the gate and it is just shy of $1000 CAD for a family of four for one day! 10 hours, 1000? Such a rip off! Come on. Why do you hate us Canadians?
Went there with my family and the top attraction was the world of Harry Potter, it was like being a part of the movies!

Universal is better than Disney hands down for older children! They also have parks for the little ones too! I’m a travel agent and we had free park to park tickets. Universal studios and Volcano bay (water park with universal) super fun! If you’re a Harry Potter fan, this is the place to go!
amazing 3D rides like transformers,the latest Jimmy fallon ride, harry potter- efg but 3 hour wait time. Must go on thrilling rides such as revenge of the mummy

You should know if there is a q line at a restaurant it going to be a long time  3 in the afternoon lines of 45 minute in restaurants we tried 3 different ones all the same  Don’t waste money on 15.99 refill cup many stations long lines then no ice in machine and warm drinks after waiting in drink line  I guess I am a long time Disney fan 300 visits in 25 years only 2 visits to Universal most-likely my last  Right after arriving the up escalator not working and had to climb 3 flights of stairs not even to the entrance yet

Stupid regulations compared Disney, almost everything forbidden for them. Very simple attractions forbidden too, despite the similar are allowed at disney and other resort around. Volcano bay is even worst!! Allais y nothing for kids. We didn’t enjoy.  Without kid is great.

Recently over the past 2 months I have ventured to the “other” Orlando theme park Universal with friends and family. Being annual pass member at the “original” Orlando theme park I have high expectations about service and experience. Universal did not disappoint on either. They are very different experiences for very different reasons. Universal does a great job of channeling people within the park. Also they have single rider lines that mover very quickly. Down side it is an expensive day for both parks. If your a Harry Potter fan it is Mecca for the enthusiast. Though you need a two park ticket to get the full experience sense the HP experiences are in both parks. The visual perspectives of the different areas in Universal are amazing. If you do one thing in Orlando it should be two words...The Hulk! I recommend checking out this park who put a great shopping, food and night life right in front of the two parks called City walk is a lot more convenient than Downtown Disney is to the Disney parks.

Although this visit was originally planned for our kids...we loved it even more I think! The Harry Potter section was just the most fantastic display I have ever seen at a theme park. The rides were great, easy to get around and we were able to see most of everything in the one day that we had to do two parks. If you had more time then spend the extra day. We rode the water ride at the end of the day...perhaps do it in the middle so you can dry off better...

Park is not gay friendly. Many of the crew members are rude and have an attitude. They won't answer any questions without an attitude. My partner and I even overheard a crew member mocking us and telling the other crew members we were "the gays over there". Extremely poor for 2019. Charge slot. Express pass on Universal side is a joke. They have two separate lines to throw you into a line without everyone else anyways. Waste of money. Not the best experience do to a lack of training and personality with its employees.

I love theme parks, all of them. I first went to universal studios about 20 years ago, I loved it then but I loathed it yesterday. Mainly because I felt everything about it was based on a plan to extort money out of visitors. This may be there aim but it was relentless.  The park is split into two. Universal studios and islands of adventure.  We paid $130 each to get into universal. To buy a ticket to “que jump” was an extra $200 each! We declined. However, the number one attraction at universal is Harry Potter and the Hogwarts express. You CAN NOT take this ride unless you have a ticket for BOTH theme parks. Outrageously unfair.  There are few places to escape the heat. Restaurants tables are full of “reserved” signs, for those people who were lucky enough to know you could even reserve tables and how to do it!  You que for at least 50 mins per ride. 70 mins for Harry Potter. Apart from rides I couldn’t see what else was there to go for. All the back stage tours and family rides have gone. So your stuck if you don’t want to que.  Drinks and food are sky high in price, really sky high. And if you doubt my review, just make sure you have the $25 you will need to park before you get to the gate and pay $130 to get in!  Many theme parks in a Florida, Disney World is the number one of course. My advice? Leave Universal until last on your hols. If you have done all the others and have some cash left to spend then go. I won’t be going again.

I'd like to start by saying that the gringotts and Rockit rides are awesome.  Now, I understand that prices at theme parks are naturally higher, but my experience here was disgusting. Regular drinks are 4.19, no refills allowed. Universal sells a refill Cup for 17 Bucks (only Works for a day). That means If you are not a heavy drinker you are going to pay a ridiculous amount to drink. I think this is a very mean trap, especially for those on a budget. For comparison, a refill drink on Disney os about 3 dollars, even though they sell refills.  The employees are also less friendly than Disney Parks. Overall, better rides, Very worse service .

VIP Vacations Inc. helped me get exactly what i wanted out of my universal trip. Early access to the parks and all! I was able to get on the new Hagrid's Motor Bike ride, despite having to wait in line for close to 5 hours: it was totally worth it!

Been taking all my three children ( each one two years apart ) by myself , being the single dad for twelve years just to Disney World. It’s so darn difficult to cater to all three kid’s interests at any given time, especially single handed.... This summer, the Oldest (19 years old now ) opted out of our summer family vacation all together tradition , as he was out on the other side of the world teaching kids there his special skills . So we decided to check out Universal Studios with my seventeen year old daughter and the fifteen year old ( spoiled rotten by everyone all his life) youngest son . I was SO VERY SKEPTICAL that I might be making a humongous mistake . But boy oh boy, my lovely wife of 5 months, was so right....Both kids had a BLAST...Must day that these two have been raised as Perfect Couch potatoes 🥔 ( NOT by me....and EXACTLY opposite of my interests) Five days went by so quick and both kids seemed longing for a couple of more extra days 😳😃😃The rides were “ AWESOME “. The NEWEST addition, Hagrid’s Magical Creatures motor bike adventure in the Harry Potter world was MAGNIFICENT....Actually, to be Honest, we ALL experienced the Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey attraction to be THE P R E M O .......

Bought tickets from the official office. Explained that we wanted one day at each park, plus a half day at each, but not bothered about the Hogworts Express ride. Was told that a 4 day ticket was best option and that on day 3 we could use a day in each park. When we tried to do this today we were told that we couldn’t without paying another $50 each. 3 rides had been closed due to ‘technical difficulties’ for the whole day (including Spider-Man which is indoor) It was pouring with rain, and we had only 3 hours left in the park - all we got from customer services was that we had been given incorrect info when we were sold the tickets. No apology. No compromise. Just pay $50 or go away. We will go away and not come back. The food was also appalling. After 20 years of visiting every year, we will not be giving you our cost on again. Shockingly bad treatment of your guests.

My wife and I have been coming to Orlando (Disney World), since we were little. The is our second time at Universal Studios - Island of Adventure and our kids first time. We were so excited to bring them here but we will NEVER return. I was so disappointed with Guest Relations and customer service we received from the staff through the entire park.  The day started off when we first attempted to get our daughter a medical pass from the Guest Relations in the front of Universal Studios. We explained to Guest Relations that our daughter has a rare syndrome called POTS (Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome) and she is unable to stand or sit for long periods of time because her blood doesn’t circulate properly. She has to drink 100 oz of water a day which of course means she has to use the restroom more often. She also overheats quickly which causes body tremors and passing out. When we explained our daughters medical condition we were offered a wheelchair. We told Universal that we were able to get an extra fast pass at Disney allowing us to be “virtually” in the line for any ride. Guest Services proceed to tell us that they’re a newer park than Disney, more ADA compliant and more accommodating. We tried to understand how Universal “believes” they’re more “accommodating” when they only offer a virtual line pass for 3 of their rides. We decided to enter the park and speak with someone else in the park that might be able to assist us and understand our daughters medical condition.  Our second attempt at Guest Services was near Men in Black with a supervisor named William. We explained our daughters medical condition and all William kept saying was I am not a medical professional, I don’t understand, help me understand what you need, we offer a variety of accommodations. We kept saying the same thing over and over. If he is not medical trained then how can he deny our request? How is this person a supervisor? He said they can offer us a wheel chair or we can spend money to purchase their “express pass”. What is really frustrating is they kept saying we don’t judge anyone based on how they look but having gone thru this experience they clearly do. We asked for a supervisor and he told us we had to go back to the front the park to find one, no assistance was offered and wouldn’t provide a managers name we can talk to. He was so rude and nasty he made our daughter so upset that she started to cry. Since our daughter doesn’t have a visual medical condition they made an assumption that we were trying to “cheat the system” and get the express pass for free. We simply wanted to have the ability to virtually wait in line on all rides, not just 3. My daughter wasn’t able to ride several rides because they would not accommodate her medical condition.  I have one question for you Universal. How has Disney, Bush Gardens, Kings Dominion figured this out? Shame on you for treating people with disabilities/medical conditions different and trying to up sale customers with a disability/medical condition to buy your express pass. The entire experience was a complete disappointment and maybe it’s because we are used to the service we receive at every Disney park.  Universal CEO and other senior management how would you like your families treated this way?  We will never return and I am severely disappointed to have spent so much money on admission and money in your park.

This was our 6th visit to Universal Orlando. Always had a great time until this vist.We found the staff much less helpful than previous visits. The new locker system was also an ordeal and the staff at them less than helpful or friendly. I contacted customer service by email to give my option. That didn't go well either and after waiting 4 weeks for a reply to something UNIVERSAL asked me for I tried again. Was fobbed off. As I said disappointing.  On a positive note Hagrid ride wad great.

Completely not what we expected. Haunted houses not even as good as ones in my city. Wait time was hour plus on each and 100 minutes on Stranger Things. To upgrade to fast pass was $130 each when tickets were $60 to begin with. Ridiculous. No maps or signs to indication direction of attraction. We've been coming to the Universal theme parks in Florida for many years. The roller coasters, waters rides and entertainment are good. This was the first and last time we ever come to this park! Unless you have fastpasses which cost you almost the price of the general admission ticket, they treat you like a 2nd class citizen. Our family of 6 spent over $700 on the park tickets this past Friday and we rode on 3 rides! The fastpass holders get treated like royalty, they don't wait even a minute, and the general line could stand for over an hour or 2 for a ride like harry potter. My husband and my older boys stood in line to harry potter ride for 2 hours, when they got close to the gate, the guy opened it, told them to go and take pictures, while they were taking those photos, which they didn't ask or need, it was bad enough that the fastpass line just endlessly goes in, he let the people in the general line go and by the time the photos were done the people who were in the back of them initially, were already in! This was our first trip to Florida and Universal, needless to say, I doubt that we will go back there. The admission was expensive enough but then they add an extra fee for a fast pass. I understand that you can't predict the weather and safety is important but they should have some kind of proceedure in place for bad weather to get guests out of the ride line and give them some kind of pass to enjoy the ride at a later time. We could have been given a pass and apology after 30-60 minutes max and been able to enjoy the rest of the time at the park. Instead we were told the park is closing in 15 minutes here is a pass to come back at a later time. No apology and rude employees when they were questioned by several guests about policies and proceedures in regards to weather.

Please make sure they get spoken to as no one should be treated like that.

We have been to HHN at universal studios several times. Our Disney/Universal expert, Robyn, with Dream Makers Vacation Services, really came through for us on this trip. When we plan a trip to Disney world, we usually set aside a day for Universal. But many things disappointed me this time and I wanted to post this review to have people consider if they really want to spend the money for a day there. At least so your homework. 1) First if all - if you want to see all of Happy Potter - you will need to pay to get into 2 parks. We payed $185.31 ($174+tax) for a 2 Park one day ticket per person. It costs more if you buy at the ticket booth in the park. I used a mobile delivery and had the ticket delivered to my smartphone. That’s a lot of money for a family of 4.  2) This time of year - the park is only open until 7pm. A lot of ground to cover for 2 parks and considering how much you are paying g for a ticket. 3) So you would expect the rides to be in good working condition. Especially the widely popular Harry Potter section. When we got there, the 2 rides in IOA: the new Hagrid’s Motorbike ride was closed. Harry Potter and the forbidden journey was experiencing delays. So we headed to The Eacape from Gringots ride at Universal. Wait was posted as 55 minutes. The line went slowly. We wished we had our backpack with some drink and snacks - but we had to put it in a locker ! We got to near of the end of the line after waiting in the queue for more than a 90 minutes and they “flushed the queue” due to technical difficulties! They did give us a FP on the way out - but it didn’t seem to cover the time lost (I could have went on 3 Other rides), sore feet and back from waiting in line that long (hey that’s messing with my Health and ability to do other things as a result of pain); needless to say - everyone was very upset. Not to mention that the People in line flooded the streets and now everything else was impossible to get into. Even Hogwarts express train - wasn’t an express and had a 55 minute wait. So we quickly Rushed to the Leaky Cauldron - which had really filled up. We were able to get some good food and rest a while. My Cottage pie came with a salad and was very good. We also got the bangers and mash - and my so. And his GF enjoyed those. Hubby got the fish pie and enjoyed that. We also got a kids Mac and cheese with a side of grapes and applesauce which also was good. They do seat you - maybe because it was busy. But we ended up getting a seat against the wall that was quiet. After we were done - we checked the time for Hogwarts Express - and it was still long ! So we headed to the front of the park where we could use the Front entrance to switch to the other park (IOA) since the Hogwarts Express lube was too long.. Disappointing. I used the opportunity to visit with guest relations.  4) Guest relations and what they can do: I’ll start out by saying the young woman who assisted us was very nice. However, the best she could do was offer us each another FP. I would have preferred a partial refund or another FP. I also brought up the fact that we had to pay for a locker for the ride - she didn’t bring it up on her own. Practically had to beg to get the $2 back. But She did give us $2 cash.  5) which brings me to the lockers. Most of the thrill rides have the lockers. It’s a pain and time consuming to get your stuff in and out. It requires the code from your ticket - but the code doesn’t work from a smartphone and you need to get a paper one from an attendant in the area. On top of that - If you need a Large locker - you need to pay $2 for it. We had a large backpack -So we had to pay it. They don’t take cash. You need a credit card. And you need to spend this $2 for each ride !!! What a way to make even more money after robbing you the cost of your ticket !  6) we finally got into IOA thru the front entrance. We bypassed the Incredible Hulk and the Spider-Man ride so we could get to the back of the park to check out the Wizarding world of Harry Potter before it was dark. On the way - we also noticed the King Kong ride was partially outside. So after taking some pics in Harry Potter world I’m the daylight - we back-tracked to the Skull Island King Kong ride instead of using a FP to ride Harry Potter and the forbidden journey. Since the line was long and the ride is inside, we figured we could come back. We waited a little while in the FP King Kong line - and it was very cool - albeit a bit shorter than I expected.  7) the Hagrid motorbike line was over 100 minutes and had closed on and off thru the day, so...  8) we went back to Harry Potter to find the Forbidden Journey ride closed !! It was 6pm and they were closing in an hour and we had not ridden any Harry Potter rides! We made a bee-line for the Howard’s express - but we first had to wait in line to go thru the ticket line to go to the other land in Universal. After waiting for 10 minutes in the ticket line we the. Went to wait in the Hogwarts express line. I checked the wait times one more time to see if Escape from Gringots might have reopened - holding out little hope - since it was closed most of the day after our wait. Miraculously it was open with a 25 minute wait. We made a bee-line to it after our Hogwarts express ride. We barely made it Into line at 6:58. And after waiting the allotted time - we finely were able to ride the ride! So we didn’t go home totally disappointed.  8) on a positive note - after we were done the ride - we wandered around a mostly deserted Diagon Alley. We also finally saw the dragon breath fire. The dragon didn’t breathe fire thru the day. Which is another negative. I believe the dragon breathed fire all thru the day when we were there last 5 years ago.  Thru the day we also managed to go on the Mummy, MIB and the Simpsons.  That’s 7 rides in 8.5 hours. That’s $26.47 a ride. I guess you have to also account for lunch and ambiance... but still... I can understand that the new Hagrid ride might be done because it’s new - but the other 2 have been around for over 5 years ! They shouldn’t be down. If they need maintenance - please do the maintenance in the Off-hours when no one is in the park. Also note that I read that one of the Harry Potter rides will be down for maintenance Jam 16-17 - so consider that if you plan to go on either of those days.  9) did i mention that you can save some time and get FPs for all the rides by staying on property ($$) or buying a FP ticket for all the rides for a mere $96 on top of what you’re paying already... thanks Universal ...  10) we won’t be going back any time soon. The old rides we’ve done and we’ll wait for the Harry Potter rides to be fixed or for the popularity to wean... if you really need to go - I recommend you do your homework. Download the “Universal wait times” app and monitor it a few days prior to going... check and see thru the day if the rides remain up. And buy your tickets online a day or so before you plan to go when you know the weather will be good and the rides are running. You can use the ticket they send you to your email from your phone.  Good luck !  ... And I hope to see some better ticket discounts and or longer hours from Universal for their customers. Otherwise I believe they are just thinking of making the most $$ for themselves.

We visited Universal Studios in late July to celebrate our daughter's HS grad. We want to commend Universal for how safe they made us feel at the parks, hotels and on citywalk. Everyone kept their masks on, socially distanced and kept things clean. The only part I would have them improve on is the hand sanitizer they use in the parks smells very bad. Disney's hand sanitizer is like purell and adds something to it to make it smell pure or good. I think they must be using a cheap version and I would say for them to review what type they are forcing people to use as it stinks and feels terrible on your hands. We didn't stay at a hotel this time to get the free Universal Express as there were no huge lines. We rode rides multiple times and had a great day. There are places to rest if you want to take off your mask and eat/drink and I would advise to do a sit-down lunch. We ate at the Leaky Cauldron and the only part that was strange is you are seated and order at your table as they don't want lines outside otherwise everything was really good. The only other suggestion for Universal in general is stop making people use lockers on rides like Men in Black. I do like the new locker system since our last visit to get your items in/out as it was much quicker than the thumb scan but make sure you keep your park ticket with you to reopen your locker. Weekdays are less crowded than weekends if you are from out of town like us.
